comment: Delivered work packages. A capability may only be advertised in misa / compiler -march / reference capability once every implementation task named for it in config/capability_ladder.json appears here. An ID is added only after that package's own registered cases have been run from a clean build and observed to pass; the evidence column records what was run and where the log lives. In particular the DUT-side evidence for I-005 and I-006 includes mutants that were rebuilt and confirmed to FAIL, because a test that cannot detect a defect it claims to cover has verified nothing.

I-016.notes: Case PASS through the official runner with the pre-existing cases `retire.head_block_and_dual`/`commit.head_block_and_dual` unchanged in scope. Seven mutants (the six original plus MOSAIC_ROB_MUTANT_GEN_LOW_BITS_ONLY) each rebuild, differ from the shipping binary and exit 1. I-014.notes: Both cases PASS through the official runner; the single-width case is the pre-existing one and is evidence that a group of one behaves exactly as before. Six mutants each rebuilt, shown to differ from the shipping binary, exit 1 with a 0->1 failing-check delta; the six I-013 mutants were re-demonstrated at their documented first mismatches, so the two-wide refactor preserved the earlier evidence. A real defect was found and fixed in the file: the second commit lane's supersede test compared lane 1's tag with itself (a continuous assign reading a variable assigned in the same always_comb block sees the settled value), so a dual retire released no mapping and leaked one physical tag per two-wide retirement; it survived because the retire case never checked the rename free set. NOT verified: profile p0 only; a checkpoint presented in the same cycle as an allocation is still a known corner (assigned to the lane as a follow-up, since the integrated core takes a checkpoint per branch dispatch); journal_overflow under a two-wide group is argued rather than run. Round 3 of the mutant re-verification independently confirmed all 6 two-wide mutant rows (exit 1, exactly the claimed first mismatches and per-row check totals 9/13/5/9/11/11 at abort) and additionally caught two mutants in the live RTL that no package report claims: MOSAIC_RENAME_MUTANT_CKPT_ALLOC_LEAK (twowide/random:1890, a checkpoint allocation leak) and MOSAIC_RENAME_MUTANT_NO_BOUNDARY_CHECK (squash_accepted expected 0 got 1 at cycle 5831 in the twowide-ckptbad phase). Both are now covered by this case and by I-013's. Recorded drift, not a defect: the package report's section 5 base numbers (9750/9818/16 checks, 'seven two-wide phases') are stale -- two checkpoint phases were added after it was written and the live figures are 9767/9843/18 -- and its sha256 prefixes no longer reproduce because the case sources changed. The mutant claims are what the record rests on and they are confirmed; the stale base figures are noted here rather than silently re-pinned. Record corrected: this entry listed rename.single_width_ownership as one of its cases, but the registry declares that case as I-013's. Both cases do exercise the two-wide module's rules incidentally, which is why the pre-crash record listed both; the case attribution systematically follows the registry, and a ledger-registry consistency audit run on 2026-10-01 flagged it. The I-013 entry is the one that claims that case. FOLLOW-THROUGH (user-directed architecture batch): the two-wide rename path this package delivered is now USED. Dispatch can allocate, read operands for and insert TWO macros per cycle when the queues have room, and the 2-entry decode buffer became an 8-entry decoded-instruction queue. The paths that stay one-wide do so for named reasons: memory macros (a single memory insert port whose operands are captured at insert), system macros (resolved at the architectural boundary), vector macros (the engine holds one macro in flight), control transfers (allocated alone so the single in-flight-branch barrier stays one bit), and a pair whose two macros target the same cluster. THE MEASUREMENT DISPROVES THE HYPOTHESIS THAT MOTIVATED IT, AND THAT IS THE RESULT: two-wide allocation does not engage on any workload, because every workload is FETCH-BOUND. The fetch unit accepts a response on only 22-25% of cycles, so the front end delivers about 0.2 instructions per cycle and the allocation rate EQUALS the fetch-response rate exactly (0.207, 0.104, 0.054 on the three workloads); the decoded queue, the dispatch queue and both issue queues sit nearly empty, and the wide-pair path is never even offered (off% = 0). A purpose-built backlog workload (pair_burst, backed up by the slow shared MUL/DIV) does fill the queues and the two-wide INSERT fired three times, but allocation still stayed one-wide because the backlog pins the queue head at 7-8 entries where no slot frees. IPC is therefore unchanged on the ALU chain (0.206), which was the falsifiable prediction that failed -- honestly, with the reason. THE BINDING RESOURCE IS INSTRUCTION FETCH (L1I hit/miss latency plus the one-request-at-a-time handshake: response 22-25% of cycles against requests at 46-50%), which is precisely the memory lane's subject, and this entry's expectation for that lane is now stated so it can be checked: the geometry work should lift the fetch response rate, and THIS change should then engage. The front end is otherwise sound in the real tree: ACT4 stays 127/127 (verified by the lane) and the whole p1 corpus passes; perf.equal_resource_compare was red at the time only on park reachability with the memory lane's in-flight rewrite present, and is re-run after that lane lands. Three mutants were built; the FIRST (swap pair order) is reported as inert on the pair path because two-wide allocation never engages -- the lane says so rather than counting it, which is the right call and the same rule the project applied to its earlier vacuous controls. NOT covered: the claim that the issue queues would bind at a higher allocation rate is untested (they never become binding at this front-end rate), and the ROB's two-wide refusal path is unexercised because the ROB never fills. 2026-10-02: the same-cycle second insert (head1_fire, the c0_from_h1/c1_from_h1 operand muxing and the lane-1 PRF/operand blocks, 112 lines) was HELD and deleted after retire.width_and_order (V-013) failed with it present; the depth-8 decoded queue and two-wide ALLOCATION ship, both proven safe by three selective builds from deleted directories (NO_INSERT PASS, NO_PAIR PASS, insert-kept-with-allocation-removed FAIL). The classification experiment shows the defect is in the retire/ROB lane-1 path that the insert exposes, not in the insert's own alloc2 identity. Lead re-ran frontend.width_buffering: PASS (p1, 22 s) in the held configuration. 2026-10-02 (final): tools/run_frontend_controls.py is green and reconciles the held state -- RESULT required=3 caught=2 inert=1 (alloc2_total=28, pairs_total=0): DROP_PAIR_TAIL and NO_BYPASS caught (exit 1, distinct hashes), SWAP_PAIR_ORDER INERT because the pair path is held (it WAS caught with the insert present, alloc2_total=34 pairs_total=100, exit 1, and is held with the feature to be re-armed when the insert returns). The suite now takes an exclusive flock on build/<profile>/unit/frontend_controls.lock: two concurrent runs sharing frontend_mut produced contradictory measurements and intermittent C++ build failures (one run deleting the other's generated files mid-compile), which is recorded in the report rather than left as a mystery.

I-022.notes: Case PASS with 93878203 checks over 199800 cycles (up from 56848546 before the audit: the uop_meta_t fields are now compared per grant and per slot, so the check count rose rather than the coverage shrinking). Audit findings: the randomised phase consumes the whole remaining cycle budget by design and compares every cycle; a directed refused-insert phase was added and the previously undiagnosed 'does a refused insert advance the allocation pointer' question is now covered by a permanent mutant MOSAIC_IQ_MUTANT_REFUSED_INSERT_ADVANCES; zero phase assertions read a live port after the clock edge (one violation was found and fixed). I-017.notes: Both cases PASS (the second is the card-named alias for the same binary), 469499 per-cycle shadow comparisons at seed 1. Seven mutants each rebuilt, shown to differ from the shipping binary, exit 1 with a +1 first-failure delta. The verdict on the original failure: the DUT was right and the testbench was wrong -- the module decides head_trap on the head alone (not gated on completeness, and taking priority over a recovery flush), events follow the ack rather than the request, and a flush cycle retires nothing. Two mutants that previously produced a zero delta are now detected because the case gained a per-cycle retire_req comparison: a mutant that cannot fail is not evidence, and this package turned two of them into real ones. NOT verified: no external reference model (the oracle is the in-file shadow plus the real ROB and rename); no RTL lint from this package (no RTL changed); the soak is 4000 random steps, not exhaustive. Second case, same task, added by the fix wave: core.event_payload passes from a clean build (checks=27, 484 comparisons, 64 events, 63 retires, 9 stores, 8 CSR instructions, 1 trap, 232 cycles). It fixes the three defects the V-013 verification reported and deliberately left to their owner. (1) LWU (OP_LOAD funct3 110) was refused by the decoder although RV64I requires it and the reference model implements it -- a program containing lwu stopped the machine; the source comment claiming 110/111 are reserved was wrong for 110 and is corrected; decode.rv64im_reserved now covers the legal encoding (166734 instructions, 82915 legal, 83819 illegal, 0 mismatches) and core.event_payload executes a real lwu. (2) The core tied the retire instance's store and CSR payload to constant zero, so the architectural event stream could not carry ev_store_*/ev_csr_* even though the frozen V-008 schema declares them -- the F-4 gap named at freeze time, now measured and closed for the RETIRE record's memory group. (3) A system-instruction trap (ECALL) published no lane-0 event at all, so a consumer saw the PC jump to the handler with nothing explaining it; the sys_trap_q path now publishes its event with the cause and pc the trap entry uses. Six mutants each fail by name, including LWU_ILLEGAL in both cases, NO_STORE_PAYLOAD, STORE_SIZE_WRONG, NO_CSR_PAYLOAD and SYS_TRAP_NO_EVENT. Fourteen other cases were re-run green, including retire.width_and_order (whose store-identity observation moved from 0 to 11 bits), the whole corpus sweep, and the event contract in both modes with its 33 negative controls intact; the schema gained reconciliation F-6. A pre-existing build break was found and fixed on the way: decode.rv64im_reserved did not build on the starting tree because mosaic_decoder_tb's flattened o_ctl_bits was 134 bits while decode_ctl_t is 135 after is_wfi was added -- verified pre-existing by linting the decoder at git HEAD. STILL ABSENT and stated: MEM_VISIBLE has no DUT-side producer (schema F-4 is unchanged -- the fix produces the RETIRE record's memory group, not the separate visibility record); an asynchronous interrupt still publishes no lane-0 event (only the sys-trap path was in scope); ev_insn/ev_pc_after/ev_trap_epc remain declared-but-absent (F-3) with the trap's epc expressed through pc_before; mtval is 0 for a system illegal-instruction trap (a neighbouring defect not taken on); csr_value is the CSR file's read-back, so a CSR whose write is forwarded elsewhere (mip) would report that unit's value. 2026-10-02: a LATENT DEFECT was found in the lane-1 path by the same-cycle insert experiment. With the insert kept and only the retire-side lane-1 request forced to zero, the program-order comparison PASSES and the event-110 wrong-PC/lane-1 failure disappears (sha 86c526da628a61a3, exit 1 only on the case's own two-slot coverage requirement). This case set remains PASS in the shipping configuration (V-013 PASS: checks=1195 events=119 retires=118 comparisons=973 dual=28 single=63 cycles=573, binary sha256 55021a58555ae419), because the broken path cannot be exercised without two-wide allocation; the defect is recorded as an OPEN ITEM against this package rather than a retraction, and it is what must be fixed before the held insert can return. Root-cause line not yet found.

I-010.notes: Case PASS from a clean rebuild (169534 checks over 166733 instructions: 82384 legal, 84349 illegal, 1443 named reserved checks). I-028.notes: Case PASS from a clean build (build/p0/unit/<case> removed first). Six mutants each rebuilt, shown to differ from the shipping binary, exit 1 with a +1 first-failure delta: stale response accepted; identity matched on the id alone without the generation; latency collapsed to one cycle; credit not returned on a kill; request/response sharing one channel (the circular-wait blocker); identity dropped from the response. The header states the recycling rule the card demands: a killed request's entry may be handed to the next request, so a late response is matched against the pairing table and dropped as stale and counted (o_stale_rsp_ctr) rather than delivered. I-033.notes: Case PASS from a clean build: 83805 checks over 4118 cycles, 336 loads, 181 stores, 332 memory transactions, 185 misaligned traps, 50 access faults, 517 responses. The RTL (written by the integration lead, verified by an independent lane) was found correct and was not edited; two defects found were in the testbench and were fixed, both by deciding from the specification rather than from the DUT: the memory model wrote the payload's low byte instead of the byte in the lane the address selects (the module's documented lane convention says the byte at addr is lane addr[2:0]), and a hand-written sign-extension constant for a signed halfword was wrong while both the DUT and the model's own SpecExtract agreed. All four mutants exit 1 with a named first failure and a check-count delta against the base 83805: NO_MISALIGN_CHECK caught at cycle 295 (a misaligned access is forwarded to memory instead of trapping), NO_SIGN_EXTEND at cycle 17, NO_STORE_SHIFT at cycle 35, FAULT_AS_ZERO at cycle 259. NOT verified: no physical memory (a byte-array model: no SRAM, cache, MMIO, coherence or ECC); single outstanding transaction only (I-043 is out of scope); don't-care fields (wstrb/wdata on a load, rsp.data on a store or fault) hide any defect confined to them; only size codes 0..3 driven; one hart; seeds are 400 random transactions, not an exhaustive proof.

I-018.notes: Both cases PASS from clean builds (build/p0/unit/<case> removed first), 419470 per-cycle comparisons over 6810 cycles in the base run. Nine mutants each exit 1 with a distinct named first failure and a delta; two of the previously delivered mutants did not elaborate at all and had never been run (they were re-expressed so they build and still inject the described defect) and three more were added so that each RTL defect fixed has a mutant failing on the check written for it. Root causes the package found: an allocation at the undo bound was accepted while the journal index wrapped (out-of-bounds write, found with AddressSanitizer -- this was the cause of the changing first divergence the integration lane kept seeing, not a shifting model); a restore undid only the restored checkpoint's own branch tag, leaking one tag per killed younger checkpoint; alloc_seen/last_alloc_gen were not reset so the first ROB_ENTRIES allocations after reset reported a regression on a compliant producer; and the credit kill was by epoch-only, which kills older work the squash does not own -- plan section 1.3 and the card forbid it, so the module's documented rule was wrong and its header was corrected rather than only its code. NOT verified: the module still owns its own copy of the speculative maps, free list, generation table and journal; the rename/recovery cutover (one owner for that state, recovery driving rename's ckpt/squash) is recorded in PROGRESS as the next integration task and is not claimed here. Third case, same task, added by the journal triage: rename.journal_window passes from a clean build (5978 shadow comparisons over 6022 cycles). The triage established the undo journal's contract from the plan and the architecture review rather than from the code: the journal holds exactly the allocations that have NOT committed, a commit removes its own entry (identity-matched on (tag, generation), never assumed from 'a commit happened'), and a checkpoint, the trap restore or a squash empties it. The refuted reading is worth recording because it was the tempting one -- 'the journal only needs the recent allocations, so retirement need not free records': the undo has to invert every allocation younger than its checkpoint, and a committed entry left in the window would hand its tag back while the committed map still names it, which is the two-owners state the module's standing invariant rejects. The defect and its fix: the window was emptied only by a checkpoint or the trap path's flush_restore, never by retirement, so a branchless stretch longer than MOSAIC_ROB_ENTRIES (64) overflowed it and o_journal_ovf_ctr was sticky -- and since one uncommitted instruction holds at most one tag and the ROB holds exactly 64, a correctly maintained window can never exceed its bound, so the flag should never be raised at all. It is now a FIFO drained by commit (a new head pointer and a per-entry generation, identity-matched on commit and on the second commit port, with the undo walking from the head), and the flag is raised only on a real clamp and cleared at every clear point and on drain-to-empty. Verified here: trap.precise_state now reports journal_ovf_seen=0 where it previously reported 1, with its cycle and comparison counts unchanged (12081 cycles, 65917 comparisons), and eighteen cases were re-run green by the lane, including all four rename and recovery cases, the six core cases and the corpus sweep. One control: MOSAIC_RENAME_MUTANT_JOURNAL_NO_RETIRE_FREE, built from a deleted directory with its -D in the build command, shipping sha256 6093b9de... against mutant 1b0efb0d..., exit 1 with the first failure 'journal-window: cycle 72: the undo window holds 64 entries but the shadow says 63'. NOT covered, stated by the lane: the clamp is unreachable at p0, so the flag's clear rules are dead logic verified by inspection only -- the case proves the flag is never raised across 255 allocations, not that a raised clamp clears; no stimulus drives a full window with a same-cycle retire; lane-1 commit matching while lane 0 does not is modelled but not directed; the drain is not driven through a two-wide allocation group; and the integrated core's checkpoint discipline is not re-proved. Two follow-ups recorded: mosaic_recovery.sv still documents its own non-draining, refusal-based window contract (correct for its mark-based window, but it is not the I-018 journal contract, and the two should not be read as one), and two rows of results/reports/mutant-reverification-2026-10-01.md's round-3 CKPT_ALLOC_LEAK evidence are now stale -- the first divergence moved from 'random: cycle 1890' to 'random: cycle 1887' because of this fix, and the report carries a note saying so.

I-021.notes: Case PASS. Five mutants re-run independently: all five exit 1. The discriminating coverage the card names is present and asserted: BTB aliasing is distinguished (two PCs colliding on one index resolve to different targets, and a retrained pair must HIT, so a predictor that always missed cannot pass), training is observable in both directions (a static predictor fails), and reset determinism is byte-identical across two runs. I-007.notes: The independent host oracle and the firmware corpus. 39 cases computed; the oracle agrees with the declared expectations and with the recorded golden signatures, and every program's three inputs produce three distinct signatures -- that last check is what stops a program whose output does not depend on its input from passing. The corpus is crt0 + linker script + trap handler + tohost/UART record + signature region, with fixed expected signatures produced on the host, not by the DUT: the failure mode the card names (comparing the DUT against values the DUT itself produced) is structurally impossible here. Exercised end-to-end by I-008's bring-up case, which compares the DUT's architectural event stream against this oracle's reference per instruction, not on an end state.

I-009.notes: Case PASS from a clean build. Seven mutants, each documented in the report with its injected defect, the phase that catches it, the check count at abort and the first failing field; the report also requires `cmp` to show the mutant binary differs from the shipping one, so a mutant built from a stale object cannot masquerade as evidence. Independently re-verified here: the base passes, and MOSAIC_FETCH_MUTANT_ACCEPT_STALE (the response accepted on the strength of the slot alone) exits 1 after 223 comparisons at cycle 17 with the report's exact first failure, out_valid(registered): expected 0, got 1. The case's discriminating coverage is the redirect path: a late response that belongs to a cancelled slot must be dropped and its credit returned exactly once, which is what four of the seven mutants target; the other three cover the outstanding-request bound, the compressed-form check and the fault path.

V-008.notes: The architectural event interface is frozen (config/contracts/event_v1.json: schema version 1, 21 fields, 100 octets per record, kinds RETIRE/TRAP/MEM_VISIBLE) and the checker is wired into `make check` in both modes; both exit 0. 33 built-in negative controls at the freeze, 36 after the version-2 revision, each one a single mutation of the interface itself, are all rejected -- the rejections name the offending field and producer rather than an aggregate count, and they cover the three-producer agreement directly: an RTL tap declaration renamed, a host record field removed, a host field widened, a codec field narrowed or reordered or dropped, a codec schema version bumped alone, and a kind table whose values disagree. The freeze is enforced at runtime too: the encoder refuses an encode whose declared version differs from the compiled schema version and the decoder rejects a differing header. Reported gaps, all explicit: no runtime encode->decode->text round trip of a live stream yet (V-010/V-013); three fields are declared pending_rtl with reasons on every run (insn_bits, pc_after, trap_epc, rule F-3); MEM_VISIBLE has no DUT-side producer yet (F-4) and the host RetireEvent must migrate to the canonical record (F-5); p0 has no cache/MSHR/MMIO event tap and no asynchronous-interrupt kind; one hart. Integration route frozen as route A (SV retire probe -> C++ canonical event -> reference adapter); route B (Difftest generator via DPI) is permitted only after the V-004/V-008 layout/timing tests and must keep the same canonical event and serialiser. ADDENDUM (2026-10-01): the interface was revised to version 2 after the freeze, deliberately and with its own report. Two things forced it: I-041 needed the retiring instruction's own length in the record (a compressed instruction's length is 2, and the event must carry it), and the schema's insn_bits field -- declared at freeze time as pending_rtl under rule F-3 -- finally gained its RTL producer, so ev_insn now maps to it and F-3 is landed rather than pending. The new insn_len field sits between insn_bits and rob_id, which moves every subsequent field by one octet (100 -> 101), so a version-1 record is not decodable by the version-2 decoder and is refused by the header check; nothing in the tree stores records, and no migration reader was written. The codec's field list, the host record, the schema's reconciliation list (F-3 closed, F-7 added) and the negative controls were all updated together: 36 of 36 illegal interfaces are now rejected, three of them new (a renamed tap declaration, a codec width that disagrees with the schema, a renamed host-record member) and three re-pointed because their mutation target moved -- none weakened, and the checker's own rule that a control which is merely present is not evidence was honoured by observing each rejection. Still pending and named on every run: ev_pc_after and ev_trap_epc have no RTL producer (F-3/F-4).

I-026.notes: Case PASS from a clean build: 956 per-cycle comparisons over 522 cycles, 11 phases, 194 completions, 23 same-bank collisions, a full 0..127 generation sweep including the 127->0 wrap, all four banks covered, and a phase in which a consumer reads the woken (tag, generation) out of the elaborated register file on the cycle after its wakeup -- the value-visibility claim observed rather than argued. Both models the case uses are documented rules, not the modules: rename's write rule and the ROB's identity-liveness rule are C++ models (the case compiles neither mosaic_rename.sv nor mosaic_rob.sv), and the durable value is read back through the PRF's own read ports. Eight mutants, each ifdef-asserted present exactly once, each rebuilt from a wiped build directory with a binary hash differing from the shipping one, each exiting 1 with a distinct named first failure and cycle: EARLY_WAKE (stale-result cycle 21, a PRF write for a stale result), SAMEBANK_DROP (cycle 75, offered != published), STALE_WRITES, DUP_WRITES, ROB_STALE_WRITES, WAKE_NO_WRITE, RT_TAG_ONLY, WR_CTR_PUB. No mutant passes identically. Independently re-verified here: the base passes with the reported numbers, and SAMEBANK_DROP exits 1 at cycle 75 with the reported first failure. One limitation recorded rather than smoothed over: the ready table keys on the numeric generation and has no reallocation input, so a generation number recycled onto the same tag while its entry is still live answers 'written' until the new producer writes. That is correct under the table's literal contract and is a cross-module width property (7-bit rename generation against the number of allocations a tag can live through), not something this module's ports can fix; it is in the RTL header and the report. NOT verified: p0 and seed 1 only; rob_cmp_bad_uop never driven; store-heavy mixes not stressed; dispatch's actual use of the ready table and the retire consumer of the stash are other packages.

I-013.notes: Case PASS from a clean build (5646 per-cycle comparisons over 5686 cycles, checks=9, base RESULT line byte-identical before, after and between mutant campaigns). Mutant evidence independently re-derived in round 3 of results/reports/mutant-reverification-2026-10-01.md against both rename cases: of 13 mutant defines in rtl/core/mosaic_rename.sv, 7 exit 1 in this case with exactly one failure at the claimed cycle and signal (NO_GEN_CHECK ownership:212, X0_ALLOC x0:1399, NO_FREE_RESTORE squash:1527, NO_EXHAUST_CHECK exhaustion:1678, NO_DUP_WB_GUARD ownership:14, NO_DOUBLE_FREE_CHECK ownership:171, plus CKPT_ALLOC_LEAK random:1890), and the 6 that pass are expected-inert here because five of them target the two-wide path (alloc2_req is never asserted in this single-width case) and one needs the two-wide checkpoint phase -- they are caught by rename.same_cycle_chain instead. Spot-checked here: NO_GEN_CHECK rebuilt and observed to exit 1 at cycle 212 with free_stale: expected 1, got 0. The ownership rule this case exists for is that a physical tag's free/owner state is only correct at its current generation, and that a recycled generation cannot make a stale release look live.

V-011.notes: ELF loader and memory-boundary verification. Case PASS from a clean build: 490 checks, 312 DUT cycles, 13 malformed images rejected and 1 accepted. The rejection contract is exit code 2 with dut_cycles=0 -- a bad image must be refused before the machine is allowed to run, which is the card's fail mode ('a wrong image keeps running') made impossible rather than merely checked. Three real loader defects were found by the new checks and fixed, none by weakening a check: e_type was never read so a dynamic ET_DYN image was accepted at its link-time address; a PT_LOAD whose vaddr+memsz or offset+filesz wrapped uint64 made a wild entry look mapped (both sums are now checked before addition and the segment containment test is overflow-safe); and p_flags was never read, so an entry inside a segment declaring itself non-executable was accepted. Six compile-time mutants each rebuild from an empty directory, differ from the shipping binary, and exit 1 naming the check they break; tools/check_elf_load.py independently re-parses the image and agrees byte for byte, and exits 1 on a corrupted manifest. Regression-checked here: harness.bad_image (I-004) and core.bringup_vs_reference (I-008) still pass and the golden signature check still agrees. Recorded judgement call: the p_flags==0 carve-out that keeps the I-004 image loadable. NOT verified: p_align is read but only the 8-byte rule is enforced; ET_NONE/ET_REL refused but not exercised against real images; the DUT checks prove image delivery and the first retire, not retire semantics or a run to TOHOST. All numbers were produced after the V-009 lane restored sim/tb/mosaic_bringup_tb.sv (wrapper sha256 78c27dfe..., HEAD 29bb23d).

V-009.notes: Reset and initial-state replayability. Case PASS from a clean build: 440 checks over reset lengths of 1, 2, 5 and 17 valid clock edges crossed with four release instants (high after the last edge, on the falling edge, low before the first edge, in a late low phase), plus abort/restart at S_FWAIT, at S_DWAIT, at the accepted TOHOST store and at a seed-chosen edge count, plus a same-seed replay of every configuration with bit-identical post-release state. The card's fail modes are the ones tested: no architectural event is reported while reset is asserted, no device write occurs during reset, and an old transaction cannot cross reset into the new run. Five negative controls all fail as required -- two in the core (an event reported in reset; mscratch surviving reset) and three in the environment model (the clear pass leaving RAM alone; an outstanding fetch/data transaction surviving reset; the end-of-run latch surviving reset). The package found and fixed a real defect in sim/tb/mosaic_bringup_tb.sv: the reset branch cleared the TOHOST-written flag but not its one-cycle commit latch, so a reset landing in that window made the restarted run report end-of-run on its first live edge with an empty event stream -- precisely the pollution the card forbids -- and the fix is guarded by a mutant that now fails, proving the line is load-bearing. It also found and fixed a vacuous abort in its own case (the TOHOST abort fired one cycle before the memory model accepted the store, so it never actually reset an outstanding transaction). Independently re-verified here: the case passes and core.bringup_vs_reference still passes. NOT verified: reset polarity as a waveform (only synchronous active-high exists in this RTL, so edge-sampled deassertion is proven but neither an asynchronous nor an active-low path); zero reset edges (undefined, the smallest tested length is 1); mcycle is excluded from the state comparison because it counts clocks, minstret is compared; privilege is carried by mstatus only because p0 is M-mode; 'queue ownership' is checked in its bring-up analogue (the memory model's outstanding-transaction state) because the bring-up core has no queue -- the package itself says this must be re-pointed at the integrated core's ROB/rename allocation state when that lands, and that re-pointing is not claimed here.

I-023.notes: The integrated core runs end to end for the first time: fetch, decode, rename, dispatch, two clusters, WB/PRF, ROB, retire and recovery are one machine and the registered case passes from a clean build -- checks=59, comparisons=678, cycles=129, retires=17, c0_alu=8, c1_alu=8, muldiv=1, max_occupied=6. The card's two fail modes are covered by controls rather than argued: MOSAIC_DISPATCH_MUTANT_SINGLE_CLUSTER (the second cluster never used) exits 1 at cycle 129 with o_c1_alu_ctr=0, and the out-of-order claim is visible in the numbers rather than asserted -- uop index 13 completed at cycle 49 while index 12 completed at 114, with retirement still in program order. Two real integration defects were found by this driver and fixed in mosaic_core.sv, both left with a negative control: the 2-entry decode buffer wrote slot 0 whenever nothing was popped, overwriting a live entry left in slot 1 by a pop, so the machine retired two instructions out of program order (observed allocation order 0,2,1); and rename's committed map was fed the ROB entry generation instead of the physical tag's generation -- same width, different counter -- so 'speculative map == committed map' was false from the first commit onward, which is the boundary every redirect and the I-018 checkpoint path rests on. After both fixes retirement order is exact and o_rename_boundary is 1 at every quiescent point. Independently re-verified here: base PASS with the reported numbers, SINGLE_CLUSTER exiting 1 at cycle 129. NOT covered, and this is a first-integration case rather than a core-complete one: no branches in the program, so the branch barrier, the redirect arbiter inside the core, cluster purge and fetch redirect are unexercised; no load/store/CSR/trap/interrupt/fence/MMIO/cache/multi-hart (dispatch refuses them and the data port is never asserted); one MUL/DIV encoding; one seed; p0 only. Two gaps stated rather than claimed: a same-cycle grant offered by both clusters never occurs (dispatch allocates one macro per cycle and alternates affinity, so the streams are staggered by construction) and the decode buffer's vacated-slot invalidation is not reached by any stimulus the lane could build -- its mutant passed and was removed rather than left in the tree as a false control. Second case, same task, added by the control-path wave: core.corpus_branch runs the corpus program p02_branch on the integrated core and passes from a clean build (checks=28, comparisons=8907, cycles=1783, retires=256, 96 control transfers of which 74 taken, 48 branches of which 26 taken, 27 JAL, 21 JALR, 35 back edges, three input patterns), with the architectural event stream compared per instruction and the signature values cross-checked against tools/host_oracle.py. That wave found and fixed four integration defects, each left with a mutant: the redirect arbiter's head gate considered only retire lane 0, so a branch retiring in lane 1 never matched the head and the core deadlocked after the program's own JAL; the fetch output register did not retire on a redirect and a dropped stale response also suppressed its drain, delivering a pre-redirect instruction and then re-delivering it every cycle; and dispatch read both operands through one port per bank, so when two sources shared a bank the second operand silently became the first (beq a0,a1 with 0x8000000000000000 against 0x7fffffffffffffff resolved taken). One mutant (MOSAIC_FETCH_MUTANT_OUT_REG_DRAG) is reported as NOT OBSERVED and is not counted as evidence. OPEN DEFECT, reported by that wave and deliberately not fixed there: reading an architectural register that has never been written since reset deadlocks the core, because rename maps it to a tag/generation that the writeback ready table never marks written, so the issue queue waits for a wakeup that cannot arrive. p02_branch writes every register it reads, which is exactly why the case passes; this is recorded as the next fix, not as a gap in the case. Third case, same task: core.unwritten_reg_read. It FIRST reproduced the deadlock the control-path wave reported -- reading an architectural register never written since reset stalled the machine for ever because rename mapped it to a tag the writeback ready table never marks written -- with a failing run recorded as the before evidence, then fixed it and now passes in 15 cycles with 3 retires (x5 reads 0x0000000000000000 at cycle 11, x6 and x7 read 9). The implemented rule is in dispatch, not rename: a source that does not address x0 and whose mapping is a tag no allocation has taken since reset reads as a defined zero and needs no wakeup, folded into the same ready-constant operand slot the AUIPC PC and the ALU immediate already use. The discriminator is rename's per-tag gen_valid, and the report explains why nothing weaker works: a tag's FIRST allocation also carries generation 0, so the reset mapping cannot be identified by (tag, generation) -- the ambiguity the control-path wave had flagged when it declined to fix this. R0 keeps its own rule and a written register always has gen_valid set, so the constant path cannot shadow a real value. Guarded by a mutant that reintroduces the defect and fails the case; fabric.fixed_two_cluster and core.corpus_branch both still pass. NOT covered by this case, stated by the lane: the two-wide lane-1 source path (the integrated core is one-wide and ties lane 1 off); I-027's operand-collector retry/latency never fires here; no rename-level check of the discriminator (the unit cases shadow-verify gen_valid, but a wrong re-implementation inside rename would be caught only by this core case and its mutants); a register written on only one path of a branch, and a RAW consumer of a folded producer, are not covered; the stall window is bounded at 2000 cycles so 'deadlocked' and 'slower than 2000 cycles' are not distinguished; loads/stores/CSRs/traps absent (the program ends in an ECALL that dispatch refuses). Fourth case, same task: core.mem_program. The out-of-order core now executes loads and stores end to end: dispatch -> LQ/SQ -> LSU endpoint, with the ROB's commit path authorising stores and redirects squashing both queues. It runs two corpus programs (p03_loadstore, p09_storeload) under three input patterns and PASSES from a clean build (checks=125, comparisons=9543, cycles=1017, retires=306, loads=63, stores=84, data transactions=147, forwarded bytes=96, memory bytes=306), with each program's signature matched against tools/host_oracle.py's independent host computation -- not against the DUT. Four mutants each fail by name, and two of them are the ones that matter most for precision: STORE_PRECOMMIT (a resident store authorised at allocation rather than retirement, so it reaches memory before its instruction retires) and MEM_BEHIND_BRANCH (a memory macro bypassing the branch barrier, so the wrong-path load at the entry branch's fall-through is issued), plus YOUNGER_FORWARDS (a load forwarding from a younger store: x5 comes back byte-swapped) and STORE_SIZE_WORD (every store told it is a word: a 64-bit result becomes 0x0000000089abcdef). Two real defects were found and fixed by this work: dispatch inserted memory macros with stale operand values -- the cluster path's value-ok test is satisfied by the issue queue filling a not-ready uop later, but a memory macro captures its operands at insert, so a store whose base register had just been written took the PRF's stale content and stored to address 0 instead of TOHOST (found by core.corpus_branch's new exit-protocol check) -- and the store queue's commit counter incremented with two separate non-blocking assignments when both commit ports fired in one cycle, so the second overwrote the first and 14 authorisations counted as 12. The four other core cases still pass: fabric.fixed_two_cluster, core.corpus_branch, core.unwritten_reg_read, and the module cases store.wrong_path_visibility, lsu.byte_forwarding and lsu.size_fault_boundaries. NOT covered, stated by the lane: store-to-load forwarding is exercised through the core only by p09 (p03 forwards nothing because its stores have already drained); the load queue's blocked-on-unknown-address and replay paths are never entered because dispatch reads every store operand before allocating, so the store queue's fill port is tied off; no faults, misalignment, partial-overlap forwarding or FENCE ordering are exercised, and p13 is not runnable without the trap path; the store queue is driven with squash_all and the narrower recovery window is wired but unused; the store event fields (ev_store_addr/data) remain unwired because the payload lives in the SQ. Still between this machine and the whole corpus: the CSR/trap path (crt0's boot sequence, p08, p13), FENCE and FENCE.I, and the late-alias/non-blocking LSU work of I-036/I-043. Fifth case, same task: core.trap_csr_program. The CSR, trap and interrupt path is now wired into the out-of-order core, and the two corpus programs that genuinely require traps run from the reset vector through crt0 on the out-of-order machine: p08_misaligned and p13_romstore, each under three input patterns, with every signature matched against tools/host_oracle.py's independent computation. Case PASS from a clean build: checks=208, comparisons=17144009, cycles=2696515, retires=428642, traps=26. The taxonomy exercised is real, not directed-only: ECALL, EBREAK, an illegal CSR read, a read-only CSR write, a misaligned load, csrrwi and mstatus WARL behaviour, plus five interrupt scenarios (timer alone, timer with software pending, timer with an external source pending, masked by MIE, and WFI halt-then-wake). Nine mutants across the three modules, each failing by name: TRAP_EPC_NEXT (a fault's mepc pointing at the instruction after the faulting one) and its mirror IRQ_EPC_NEXT (an interrupt's mepc pointing at the interrupted instruction instead of the next one), TRAP_NO_FLUSH, TRAP_NO_FETCH_REDIRECT, MRET_PC_WRONG, MRET_NO_RESTORE, NO_FIELD_MASK (a CSR write setting bits the generated mask forbids), MIE_IGNORED and PRIORITY_REVERSED. All six other core and module cases still pass: fabric.fixed_two_cluster, core.corpus_branch, core.unwritten_reg_read, core.mem_program, csr.precise_trap_mret, interrupt.boundary_replay. Two expectation relationships are stated rather than claimed as raw oracle equality, and both are checked: p08's third signature is the oracle's with the eight-record fold that trap.S's restore order produces, and p13's differs by one bit because the armed-trap recovery resumes at mepc+4 so the marker instruction after the store executes. Gaps stated by the lane: S-mode/privilege transitions are not applicable (p0 is M-only, MPP read-only); delegation is not exercisable in p0 (mideleg tied to zero, medeleg WARL-only-legal-zero); MEI/external interrupts and multiple concurrent pending interrupts can never be taken in this profile (mie[11] is read-only zero, no PLIC) and the case pins that the timer wins while the external source is pending; nested interrupts are not exercised (trap entry clears MIE and no handler re-enables it) though synchronous nesting is; the load access fault cause is wired but no corpus program takes one; cause 2 is exercised only for CSR accesses because the machine stops on an unserviceable decode; WFI with an enabled pending interrupt and MIE=1 is not run; corpus programs p01-p07 and p09-p12 are not run here. A trap-vector arming policy is stated explicitly: ECALL/EBREAK stop the machine while mtvec holds its reset value, which is what keeps the two ECALL-terminated sibling cases passing. Sixth case, same task: core.corpus_sweep. The ENTIRE p0 corpus runs on the out-of-order core and passes against the independent host oracle: 13 programs x 3 input patterns = 39 runs, 39 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 STOPPED, 17484988 cycles, 2774478 retires, every signature compared against tools/host_oracle.py's host computation (the oracle itself re-verified on the same run: it agrees with the corpus declaration, the golden file and its own input-sensitivity check). Independently re-run here from a deleted build directory with the same result. The case prints the full program x input matrix, states the SHA-256 of every RTL file it compiled (all identical before and after the work), and its failure path was exercised: a deliberately perturbed expectation makes the sweep report a mismatch with the right first divergent word. Two evidence paths now agree: p08_misaligned and p13_romstore pass in this sweep and in core.trap_csr_program. What the sweep cannot see, stated by the lane: it compares signatures, so a defect that leaves the final signature intact while corrupting intermediate architectural state (a wrong value that is overwritten before the end, a spurious retire that writes to a register nobody reads afterwards) would not be caught here -- that is what the per-slot retire comparison of V-013 and the event-stream contract of V-008 exist for, and neither substitutes for the other.

I-034.notes: Speculative store queue and store-commit authorisation. Case PASS from a clean build: 299262 checks over 3331 cycles, 112 stores allocated, 24 drained, 82 squashed, 1 faulted. The card's two fail modes are covered by controls: a store visible before commit (MOSAIC_SQ_MUTANT_VISIBLE_BEFORE_COMMIT, independently rebuilt here and observed exiting 1 after 548 checks with a wrong-path drain request) and a flush deleting an already-authorised store (FULL_FLUSH_DROPS_AUTHORISED). Seven mutants in total, each rebuilt from a deleted build directory, each with a distinct named first failure: visible-before-commit, authorised-store-dropped-on-squash, drain-duplicate, drain-out-of-order, allocation-dropped-when-full, early-visibility-before-address-and-data-ready, commit-out-of-order. The wrong-path requirement is checked against the memory side, not just the queue: the case counts memory transactions, and a squashed store produces zero. One contract change is recorded rather than hidden: the authorisation watermark was first adjusted arithmetically (+1 on commit, -1 on drain) and the soak produced the combination it cannot express -- a commit and a squash of the same entry in one cycle -- so the watermark is now derived from the cycle's survivors (the leading resident-and-authorised entries), which is the same statement as the prefix invariant; the header says so. Two testbench defects, both the same class (the lane convention describes the bus, not the memory: the memory model received the endpoint's lane-shifted payload shifted a second time, and the expected memory took the store's byte at the lane index instead of byte i at address+i), passed every directed phase because every directed store starts at lane 0 and were found by the soak's non-zero lanes; the DUT was right in both. The forward-query port is exercised every cycle against its stated rule but is consumed by nobody and carries no mutant -- it is a defined and tested rule, not a proven integration interface. NOT verified: no integration (nothing shows the ROB driving commit_valid_i with a per-store identity, or the identity/epoch wiring being right); the young-window bound is supplied by the testbench because mosaic_rob does not expose its allocation pointer, so the region rule is verified given a window, not the production source of that window; one outstanding memory transaction only; no caches/MMIO/coherence; p0 geometry only; simulation only.

V-012.notes: Fixed signature and termination decision. Case PASS from a clean build. Eight termination statuses are documented and every one is observed: PASS=0, PROGRAM_FAIL=1 (code 0x2A carried out through TOHOST), TIMEOUT=2 (a spinning program, TOHOST never written, its signature still intact), WFI_STALL=3, SIGNATURE_MISMATCH=4 (a program that self-reports PASS while word 2 disagrees with the model -- the case's own point that the self-report is not the verdict), SIGNATURE_OVERRUN=5 (an 8-byte store one word past the frozen window), UNDRAINED_STORE=6 (a store to signature word 3 five cycles after the exit pulse), IMAGE_REJECTED=7 (corrupt magic and a wrong entry point, both refused before any instruction executes). Six harness mutants each exit 1 naming its first wrong classification (TIMEOUT_IS_PASS, WFI_AS_TIMEOUT, FAIL_IS_PASS, NO_SIGNATURE_CHECK, NO_OVERRUN_CHECK, NO_DRAIN); the last one is the most instructive -- reading the signature at the exit pulse instead of after the drain fabricates a mismatch rather than reporting an undrained store. Two drain sub-rules are reported as REDUNDANCY PROBES, not evidence: this core has no store buffer, so 'the exit store retired at or after the pulse' and 'the hart is out of the data-request states' cannot fail and were never observed to. The ISA audit of all seven non-WFI programs is clean (155 instructions). A tool defect reported by this package was fixed here: tests/programs/audit/check_p0_isa.py matched forbidden symbol names as substrings of the whole objdump output, whose first line contains the image's path, so any image under a path containing 'exit' (or printf, memcpy...) was rejected for a symbol it did not contain. It now matches the symbol-name field of each symbol line (stripping -T version suffixes), and both directions were verified: an image at /tmp/exit_path_test/exit_image.elf now audits clean, while the same image with _start renamed to printf is rejected with 'symbol printf -- libgcc/libc leaked in' and exit 1; the 39-image corpus still audits clean. The package's directory workaround (tests/programs/termination/ instead of .../exit/) is left in place -- it is no longer needed but renaming it back would churn a passing case for nothing. NOT verified: the DUT here is the in-order bring-up core, so nothing in this package is evidence about the out-of-order fabric; RUN/PC_ESCAPED is a harness convention (executing from boot_rom is reported as a runaway); the signature guard band is this case's own conformance rule, not an ISA rule and not a line in config/; the six mutants are C++ harness defines, not RTL fault injection; no UART/MMIO/interrupt path exists in p0 to exercise.

I-035.notes: Load queue and store-to-load forwarding. Case PASS from a clean build: 107414 checks over 3501 cycles, 402 loads, 871 stores, 244 replays, 397 forwarded bytes, 1069 memory bytes. Five mutants, each rebuilt from a deleted build directory with its -D in the build command and a distinct named first failure; independently re-verified here: MOSAIC_LQ_MUTANT_YOUNGER_FORWARDS (the card's second fail mode, a younger store forwarding into an older load) exits 1 after 6603 checks at cycle 276 with forward mask 0x000000ff where 0x00000000 is required. The other controls cover the card's other fail mode (ALIGNED_WORD_ONLY -- comparing only aligned words, which the byte-level checks catch), ignoring the unknown-address block, forwarding stale bytes after the blocking store is squashed, and taking a byte from memory that a legal older store covers. No RTL defect was found; six testbench defects were found by the checks and fixed, all recorded, including two worth naming: the younger-store test originally used an address that older stores also covered (so it proved nothing about the youngest-older rule) and the soak squashed the store queue so often that it forwarded only 3 bytes in 3000 cycles (a passing case that was barely exercising the feature). One design fact the lane reports rather than hides: the store queue's forward query cannot express program order, so per-byte youngest-older selection reads the SQ's exported entry view while the query supplies the unknown-address block only, and the two are cross-checked every cycle against o_lq_query_mismatch_ctr. NOT verified: no core integration (nothing shows dispatch allocating loads in program order, the identity being the ROB's, or a core wiring the entry view up); one load in flight only (the endpoint is one-at-a-time; I-043 would change that); no FENCE (I-037), no speculative disambiguation or violation replay (I-036), no MMIO (I-038); faults are reported, not taken; p0 geometry only; simulation only.

V-010.notes: Clock and sampling-loop calibration -- the package that makes every other case's event counts exact, and the last gate on the base integer set. Case PASS from a clean build: three runs (zero latency and two item-by-item latency plans), 630 cycles, 45 instructions per run, with three independent tallies agreeing exactly -- the reference model's events, the event tap's records and the fetch accepts -- plus 110 checks. A repeated-sampling detector is built in: no record may be emitted twice for the same (retire_seq, pc) identity and the sequence numbers must be dense. Four harness mutants (each rebuilt from a wiped directory with its -D in the build command) exit 1 with their own named first check, including the double-eval one the detector exists for. The package also audited all thirty drivers' clocking discipline against the drive-low / eval-low / eval-rising / eval-falling / one-settled-sample convention and reported each deviation rather than rewriting other lanes' drivers: tb_harness.cpp evaluates twice in the high phase (idempotent, no input changes between them, both before the retire sample) and tb_wb.cpp's extra low-phase eval is an input change rather than a re-sample, so neither can double-count; the alu/decoder cases are combinational and have no timeline; nine of thirty drivers never call dut.final() and no sim/tb/*.sv contains a final block, a timescale, a delay, an initial block or $finish, so dut.final() executes no design code anywhere in the tree -- the card's 'missing final before the end' fail mode has no instance, and the case asserts Verilator's time()==0 and eventsPending()==false instead; --timing is enabled nowhere in the tree, so the 'pending events not advanced' fail mode has no instance either. Regressions re-run after the harness edit: core.bringup_vs_reference, reset.replay_determinism, loader.elf_boundaries, exit.protocol_termination and harness.bad_image all PASS, and V-009's five reset mutants still all exit 1. NOT verified: the audit is a reading of the drivers, not a proof about them; the detector is exercised only through this case's own runs; no other package's driver was rewritten even where it deviates. IMPORTANT follow-up recorded by the lane: dut.final() being a no-op tree-wide means the end-of-run assertion discipline the card asks for currently holds for this case only, and any future per-case final check must be added case by case. SECOND CASE, SAME TASK, added after the cache integration found the hazard: the reset-traffic rule. THE RULE: while reset is asserted a driver's bus model must not accept, queue or deliver a request, and a request the DUT presents during reset is IGNORED -- chosen over asserting a protocol error because holding the reset-vector request while reset is asserted is a legal held-PC state rather than a DUT error. IT LIVES IN ONE SHARED PLACE: mosaic::BusResetGate in sim/common/bus_reset_gate.h, included through sim_common.h, with a single MayAccept decision point and a MayDeliver gate for response pops, plus two named knobs that default OFF (observation, and a control that restores accept-during-reset). TWENTY-SEVEN core drivers were changed to route their accept and pop through it, and the survey found that six non-core drivers already carried their own ad-hoc guard -- with the honest detail that several core drivers had the rule on the instruction path but NOT on the data path, so the hazard was half-closed rather than absent. The bringup wrapper is a second, independent SystemVerilog implementation of the same rule with its own counters and control. THE CASE PASSES (39 checks) and its RESULT line states the conditions it exercised: first=nonredirect (the first post-reset instruction does not redirect, which is the condition under which the hazard bites -- a program starting with a JAL would pass even with the bug present), reset_request_cycles=8 with reset_accepts=0, the retired stream matching, and a control run in which 4 reset-time requests ARE accepted, which makes the case fail and proves it catches the class. It also demonstrates the stale-response mechanism deterministically: a queueing model that accepts the reset-vector request delivers the wrong instruction word to the post-reset request with the same id and epoch, and under the rule delivers the correct one. ACT4 is restored to 127/127 (verified here) and twenty-seven cases were re-run green, each driver's own case among them. NOT covered, stated by the lane: the vector driver tb_vec.cpp was excluded because another lane held it (it needs the same rule and the follow-up is named), and the rule's enforcement is a driver obligation -- the DUT may legally present a request during reset, so no RTL mutant expresses it.

I-037.notes: FENCE and FENCE.I in the out-of-order core. Case PASS from a clean build (checks=15, retires=33, one FENCE.I redirect, 5 store transactions, the data-ordering results matching the expectation). The rule implemented is stated as a rule and is conservative as the card demands: a fence completes only when the memory path is idle -- store queue empty, load queue empty, and the LSU endpoint neither holding nor expecting a transaction -- and while a fence is staged the single memory insert port is refused so no younger memory macro can be handed to a queue. FENCE.I adds a system redirect to its own pc+4, which advances the fetch epoch and cancels outstanding fetch slots, purges the decode buffer and ROB, flushes both memory queues and restores rename to the committed map; retire lane 1 is suppressed while a FENCE.I is at the head so the following instruction cannot retire before the redirect flushes it. FENCE explicitly does not touch the fetch view, is not a cache flush, and is not a cross-hart synchronisation. Four mutants, each failing by name and each matching a card fail mode: FENCE_EARLY (a fence completing while an older access is still outstanding), FENCEI_NO_INVALIDATE (stale instruction bytes executed -- the card's first fail mode), FENCEI_SKIP, and FENCE_ACCESS_PAST (a younger access proceeding past the fence). The case exercises self-modifying code for real and detects a stale fetch. A pre-existing defect was found and fixed while doing this: a memory macro inserted in the same cycle as a redirect survived the queue squash, so the core now refuses the insert while rob_flush_pulse is high. All eight other core and memory cases still pass. Gaps stated by the lane: cross-hart ordering cannot be exercised at all in p0 (one hart), so 'FENCE is not an automatic cross-hart I-cache sync' is confirmed by construction only; fence.tso is not distinguished from a full fence (stronger, never weaker, but not tested); the fetch unit's outstanding-request table is exercised only indirectly -- the invalidation reuses the same redirect/epoch path as fetch.redirect_late_response and the case does not read the fetch cancellation counters, so 'a slot was outstanding' is marked [INFERENCE] rather than claimed; and the load-queue conjunct of the drain rule is checked for emptiness but its ordering effect is not independently stressed, because the single in-order endpoint already forces an older load to complete before a younger store.

V-013.notes: Two-wide retirement and slot ordering compared per slot against an independent program-order model. Case PASS from a clean build: checks=1195, 119 events, 118 retires, 973 comparisons, 28 dual-retire cycles, 63 single, one same-rd configuration, one slot-0-trap-blocking-slot-1 configuration, one adjacent store/load pair, 573 cycles. Five controls (rebuilt from deleted build directories, each exiting 1 naming the check it breaks) plus three invisibility probes; the trace-gap and duplicate-identity detector is built in, and x0 is asserted unwritable in both slots under every write form the decoder accepts. The five situations the card names are produced and the case asserts its own coverage of them. NOT covered, stated by the lane: interrupt-driven retirement ordering (no interrupt is taken while a dual retire is in flight), and the 1-wide configuration is not exercised independently of the 2-wide one. The lane also reports three defects it found and deliberately did not fix, all recorded in its report section 6 and now tracked as their own package: (1) LWU (opcode 0000011, funct3 110) is refused by the decoder although RV64I requires it and the reference model implements it -- the source comment claiming 110/111 are reserved is wrong for 110, and a program containing lwu stops the machine; (2) the core ties the retire instance's store and CSR payload inputs to constant zero, so the architectural event stream carries no store or CSR identity (ev_store/ev_store_size/ev_csr_* are always 0), which is exactly the F-4 gap the V-008 interface freeze declared pending; (3) a system-instruction trap (ECALL) publishes no event at all -- the trap port asserts but no lane-0 event is emitted, so a consumer of the event stream sees the PC jump to the handler with nothing explaining it, contradicting the retire module's own header that a trap is an event in its own right. The lane ran no RTL edits, so the corpus sweep's revision hashes stay valid. Numbers updated after the package's own post-commit refinement: the case replaced its end-state comparison with literal-versus-DUT and literal-versus-model checks and in doing so found a wrong literal of its own -- an addi immediate above 12 bits is sign-extended and truncated, so the program wrote 0x777 rather than 0x7777, and the expectation had encoded the wrong value. Shipping binary sha256 b34fc7ede2414e54c5f45603796479aca180ca791903935338013dc6be24f0ee; all five controls and three probes re-run unchanged. The 1187 in this entry's first version was the pre-refinement count and is superseded rather than silently kept.

I-027.notes: Local bypass fast path. Case PASS from a clean build: 1593 per-cycle comparisons over 1645 cycles, a 32-link consecutive RAW chain measured at 1.000 cycles per link with the bypass against 2.000 without it when uncontended, and 1.000 against 7.343 per link when a competing producer from another cluster offers up to eight outstanding results. The latency figures are measurements from that run on that geometry, not design intent. The bypass preserves the producer's identity, the miss and conflict paths fall back to the durable path, and the combinational-loop question is answered structurally in the header rather than by a mutant the lane could not express. Four mutants each exit 1 with a distinct named first failure: UNAUTH_FORWARD (a value forwarded before its producer is authorised), TAG_ONLY (a different generation at the same numeric index matching), NO_FALLBACK (a miss stalling instead of reading the durable path) and EARLY_TAP (the bypass firing a cycle before the value exists). All eight other cases named by the lane were re-run green on the recorded revision, including the six core cases and the whole corpus sweep. THE SCOPE IS MODULE-LEVEL AND THE RECORD SAYS SO: the registered case names a standalone topology (`mosaic_cluster_bypass_tb`, compiling only `mosaic_cluster_bypass.sv`), so the mechanism is verified in isolation and the integrated cluster/issue-queue path is described but NOT exercised; the durable side the case compares against is the driver's model of the two real register boundaries (the result register and the arbiter's pending register) rather than the elaborated arbiter and register file, so the claim is a relative gain, not an absolute one; producer-side backpressure is not modelled, so a full result register would gate even a bypassed chain at durable throughput; the competing producer is bounded rather than calibrated; issue-side backpressure is not exercised; and the geometry is p0 with one seed and a single-cycle producer. Wiring the bypass into the live cluster is the follow-up this entry deliberately does not claim.

I-038.notes: Non-speculative MMIO. Case PASS from a clean build; the observed RESULT line reports checks=69 (the lane's summary said 70 -- the observed figure is recorded here). Two runs after full resets, each compared against an independent RV64IM interpreter and a device model in the driver: run A (correct path plus an error trap) retires 34 instructions with 5 device transactions, 6 ordinary ones, 8 serialiser hold cycles and trap cause 5 at the faulting PC with mepc/mcause/mtval all matching the model; run B (wrong path) is created by an ecall behind a slow divide that flushes two dispatched loads -- the ordinary RAM load still reached memory (ordinary traffic exactly one above the reference, so the window is real and the case proves it) while the device read did not, with the serialiser refusing device offers for 60 cycles. Zero wrong-path device accesses. The mechanism is a device serializer in mosaic_core.sv between the queue request mux and the endpoint, with three rules stated as rules: a device access is presented only when it is irreversible-safe (a load only at the ROB head at a legal boundary; a store because the store queue drains only authorised entries); exactly once, because the serializer owns the transaction in one register from acceptance to response and the requester cannot re-offer it and the load queue never replays a device load; and never coalesced, because both queues' forwarding searches skip device entries and a device load's bytes are forced from the device. The device predicate is the three non-idempotent regions of config/memory/p0.json. Four mutants each rebuilt from a deleted build directory with their -D in the command, differing in hash and exiting 1 on a named first failure: a speculative device access (pop count 2 against 1), a replayed transaction (identity 2064 seen twice), an error response swallowed (the faulting instruction retires), and the device attribute cleared (a device address presented as cacheable RAM). A combinational ready loop is argued structurally rather than claimed as a mutant: the serialiser's ready depends on its own register and the endpoint's state machine, never on req_valid_i. A REAL DEFECT was found and fixed while building this case: the core recorded the endpoint-response owner when the queues' offer was taken, which the serialiser invalidates for device requests -- at any memory latency above one cycle an older transaction's response could be delivered to the new owner; the owner is now recorded at the endpoint's own acceptance and latched with the held transaction. Thirteen other cases were re-run green, including the whole corpus sweep, the six core cases and the three memory-module cases. NOT covered, in the report: interrupts around a device access (the core's trap gate is gated on the serialiser being idle but no interrupt is driven); device-versus-RAM forwarding coalescing is unreachable by construction in this profile (the ROB-head rule drains older stores), so the coalescing control is expressed as the attribute mutant; o_mem_dmem_id is checked for uniqueness and counted rather than attributed per retiring instruction; a device that never responds would hang the memory path (no watchdog); the wrong-path window is trap-created because the dispatch barrier makes it impossible behind an unresolved branch; only the p0 memory map is covered.

V-014.notes: Synchronous trap comparison and precise state. Case PASS from a clean build: checks=167810, 65917 comparisons, 12081 cycles, 4740 retires, 35 traps across seven kinds (illegal instruction, ecall, ebreak, load misalignment, store misalignment, load access fault, store access fault) and five placements (at the ROB head, away from the head, before a long-latency instruction whose younger divide is squashed and replayed, after a long-latency instruction whose older divide is complete in the frame, and a same-cycle-completion situation), with the machine's whole RAM and all 35 trap frames compared bit for bit against an independent ISA-derived model rather than against the DUT. Six controls, two of them RTL mutants and four driver-level (each stated as such): TRAP_AS_NORMAL (a faulting instruction retiring as a success), MTVAL_MASKED (a wrong mtval being masked wholesale), REF_EXTRA_INSN (the reference taking one instruction too many), MRET_PC_WRONG, RD_POLLUTED (an exception writeback polluting the destination register first) and REPLAY_POLLUTED_REPLAY_LOST. This was the last gate on advertising Zifencei. No RTL was edited. ONE MACHINE OBSERVATION reported rather than fixed, reproduced here on my own run (journal_ovf_seen=1): mosaic_rename's undo window is emptied only by a branch checkpoint or by the trap path's flush_restore, never by retirement, so a branchless stretch longer than MOSAIC_ROB_ENTRIES (64) allocations overflows it and o_journal_ovf_ctr is sticky -- it is not cleared even by flush_restore. There is no architectural effect in this case (the trap path restores from the committed map, not the journal, and all 35 frames plus the RAM match the model), but a sticky flag would mask a genuinely clamped journal squash later in a run, so it is recorded as a maintainability defect to triage rather than as a pass. NOT covered, stated by the lane: asynchronous interrupts (no irq is asserted here; that is V-015), delegation (M-only, medeleg/mideleg canonicalise to zero), S/U mode and any privilege transition other than M, mtval for an instruction-fetch fault (the harness drives no fetch error), a same-cycle-completion situation for a system trap (structurally impossible: the macro owns the head and sys_commit is zero for every system trap), a branch-mispredict squash interleaved with a trap (the program is branchless apart from the trap path and the park loop), and compressed/F/D/V/multi-hart/MMIO/WFI/FENCE.I paths.

I-029.notes: Dynamic steering baseline policy: deterministic locality-first, then least-loaded, then age -- no predictor, no learned state. Case PASS from a clean build: 3030 per-cycle comparisons over 3118 cycles, the fixed and dynamic modes agreeing on the architectural result while differing in time (572 cycles fixed against 379 dynamic in the comparison program), which is the shape the card asks for: identical architecture, measured schedule. Three mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: IGNORE_CAPABILITY (a uop routed to an incompatible unit -- the card's first fail mode), SATURATION_ADMIT (saturation resolved by admitting work rather than stalling or retrying -- the card's second fail mode), and NONDET_AGE (a tie-break that the program's state does not explain, caught at the first unexplained decision, which is the premise of the fixed/dynamic comparison rather than an architectural difference -- the report says so explicitly instead of claiming a stronger catch). Eleven other cases re-run green, including the six core cases, the corpus sweep, MMIO, FENCE and the bypass. SCOPE, stated by the lane and recorded here: the policy is a new module (rtl/core/mosaic_steering.sv) and the lane changed ZERO lines in mosaic_core.sv, mosaic_dispatch.sv and mosaic_cluster.sv -- the shipping core still uses its alternating toggle. The policy is therefore verified in isolation; the report documents the integration point and the four things an integration needs (strategy select, producer-cluster locality, per-unit occupancy, and the capability matrix as configuration) and notes that making the shipping core use the fixed baseline would contradict fabric.fixed_two_cluster's claim. Also not covered: the occupancy the policy reads is the driver's model rather than measured cluster state; no timing/area characterisation; the 4096-macro age bound that makes the unsigned comparison exact is a driver bound, not a proof about an unbounded stream; saturation is exercised (the shared MUL/DIV queue fills to 2 of 2 with 20 stall cycles in the directed burst, and both cluster queues reach capacity in the dynamic run) but a stall caused by both clusters being full while the class has no shared fallback is not separately forced; two clusters contending for one unit in the same cycle is not exercised because this core dispatches one macro per cycle; and the SYSTEM class is only untested in the negative sense, its capability bit being clear in the matrix the driver hands over.

V-015.notes: Replayable asynchronous interrupt driving. Case PASS from a clean build: 70 checks, 549 cycles, 308 retires, 3 traps, with two runs through a reset from fresh memory models producing an identical per-cycle trace hash (0x5e5cbc99d04548e0), identical asserted and accepted boundaries, so the same stimulus replays to the same acceptance boundary -- the card's central requirement. Scenarios driven: a timer interrupt asserted at a numbered retirement boundary while both mie[7] and mstatus.MIE are clear (75 cycles pending-and-disabled and 85 cycles enabled-but-MIE-clear, with no offer in either window); an enable CSR written in the immediately preceding instruction (csrw mie,0x80 at 0x800001a8, accepted at the next boundary with mepc=0x800001ac); the same masked interrupt not lost but taken at the first boundary the enable opens; a synchronous trap competing with an interrupt (a software interrupt pending, enabled and unmasked at an ecall that is itself the head -- the interrupt is taken first and the ecall traps afterwards, each exactly once, with the same mepc); a WFI halt that an external interrupt does not wake but a timer at the halt threshold does; and the p0 external interrupt pinned as structurally inert (mip/mie bit 11 are read-only zero, so the case records the inertness rather than inventing an acceptance). The 'an interrupt is not an instruction' rule is checked directly: retired_in_cycle is zero at every interrupt trap cycle, o_commit_o equals the published retirement events, irq_valid implies MIE and an enabled pending bit, and the spurious-wake counter never moves. Three mutants each exit 1 naming its own first failure: WALLCLOCK (injection keyed on host time -- boundaries 39 against 33 and a different trace hash), ORDINARY_RETIRE (an interrupt counted as a retiring instruction), and LOST_PENDING (an unaccepted interrupt dropped). NOT covered, stated by the lane: the external interrupt can never be taken in p0 (its bits are read-only zero), so inertness rather than acceptance is what is pinned; the 'exception already captured on the head' priority branch is not exercised because the interrupt is taken as soon as a boundary opens; two interrupts pending and enabled at once is not driven here, so the MEI>MSI>MTI order is not re-derived (I-020 covers it exhaustively); software writes to mip, mideleg (zero in p0), and multi-hart are out of scope; and the WFI wake is keyed on the halt's duration rather than a retirement boundary, for the structural reason that a halted hart retires nothing.

I-030.notes: Queue/port quotas and a starvation bound. Case PASS from a clean build: 62593 per-cycle checks over 3414 cycles. Four classes with declared quotas (SCALAR 4 of a window of 8 grant opportunities, MEMORY 2, MULDIV 1, VECTOR 1) and a measured worst-case wait per class compared against a bound computed from the run's own numbers (SCALAR 17 against 54, MEMORY 33 against 78, MULDIV 55 against 126, VECTOR 55 against 126 cycles), with share_min measured as exactly the declared quotas and gap_max as 3. The card's hard requirement -- an explicit fairness assumption rather than an infinite timeout -- is met and CHECKED: the assumption ('while the arbiter has pending work the port is not ready for at most 4 consecutive cycles, equivalently the downstream becomes ready within that bound') is written into mosaic_arbiter.sv's header and exposed as o_busy_run_max plus a sticky o_assumption_violated; the case fails named 'assumption' if the stimulus violates it, and a dedicated phase holds the port not-ready for seven cycles and requires the DUT to report a violation rather than a bound. The stimulus provably reaches the card's fail mode: on the same offer stream a naive strict-priority control serves SCALAR 2400 times and leaves MEMORY, MULDIV and VECTOR requests unserved. Three mutants each exit 1 naming a distinct first failure: STARVE (strict class priority starves VECTOR), DROP_ON_QUOTA (the escape pops and discards instead of delivering -- loss instead of backpressure) and REQ_ID_SERVICE (service charged per requester change, so the bound is not computable). Four further seeds pass with the same shape. Independently re-verified here: the case passes from a deleted build directory, and it compiles only rtl/core/mosaic_arbiter.sv, so it is unaffected by other lanes' in-flight core edits. SCOPE, stated by the lane: the policy is a new module and the live core's writeback/issue arbitration is not yet routed through it -- wiring it in is part of the fabric integration that also covers I-027's bypass and I-029's steering, and that integration is recorded as outstanding rather than implied by this pass. NOT covered: the vector class does not exist as real hardware yet (I-049..I-063), so the class it protects is modelled; the bound is computed from this geometry; no timing/area characterisation.

I-039.notes: The A extension's atomic path. Case PASS from a clean build: 699 checks. All nine AMO operations are covered at both widths (AMO*.W and AMO*.D) with signed and unsigned boundary operands -- which is the point of the card's signedness requirement -- plus aq and rl variants. The atomicity rule the card demands is implemented as a single read-modify-write at a shared serialization point rather than as a loose load+store pair: the request carries an operation class (MEM_AMO, a third kind beside load and store, precisely because treating it as either would either write memory speculatively or return a stale value), and the endpoint performs the read and the write as one indivisible step. Three mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: SPLIT (the read-modify-write decomposed into a load and a store, losing atomicity), IGNORE_AQR (aq/rl treated as performance hints rather than ordering), and MINMAX_SIGNED (a signed/unsigned boundary taken from the wrong operand's signedness). Independently re-verified here after the tree was restored. NOT covered, stated by the lane: LR/SC are deliberately left illegal (they are I-040's); the competing agent is a cooperative second master on the port rather than a second hart, because p0 is single-hart; aq/rl are carried into the memory transaction and their ordering holds structurally (ROB-head serialization, store-priority mux, in-order load queue) but the case does not exhibit a relaxation that aq/rl would forbid -- it verifies the bits reach the transaction and that no younger access sits between the beats; misaligned AMO (which must trap, cause 6) and AMO to a device are not driven; I-036 disambiguation and store-to-load forwarding into an AMO are not exercised; and no corpus A-extension program exists, so the case assembles its own image.

I-041.notes: RV64C decompression and cross-boundary fetch, delivered on the second attempt. Case PASS from a clean build: 98 checks over 11 runs, hand-built images compared against the driver's own RV64IC reference. The encoding groups are implemented in the decoder with the reserved set refused as exactly CTL_ILLEGAL (quadrant 0 c.addi4spn/c.lw/c.ld/c.sw/c.sd; quadrant 1 c.nop/c.addi/c.addiw/c.li/c.lui/c.addi16sp/c.srli/c.srai/c.andi/c.sub/c.xor/c.or/c.and/c.subw/c.addw/c.j/c.beqz/c.bnez; quadrant 2 c.slli/c.lwsp/c.ldsp/c.jr/c.mv/c.ebreak/c.jalr/c.add/c.swsp/c.sdsp), with hints legal and non-trapping and the F/D forms refused as unimplemented. Length and original bits travel from the decode through the descriptor and the ROB to the architectural event record, so the card's central rule holds by construction: a compressed instruction's PC and length are its own, never the previous PC plus four, and a compressed jump's link value is pc+length.
