Four controls each exit 1 by name: FETCH_PC_PLUS4 (the card's named fail mode), DELIVER_16BIT (length reported as four), C_RESERVED_EXEC (a reserved encoding executed instead of trapping) and IMEM_MUTANT_WRONG_LINE (a straddling instruction assembled from the wrong line). THREE DEFECTS were found and fixed on the way. (1) The regression that failed the first attempt: a speculatively fetched reserved encoding -- the zero padding behind the corpus text's final jal -- reached dispatch and stopped the machine *before* the still-in-flight jump could redirect and squash it, and the redirect was itself gated on not-stopped, so the deadlock was complete; dispatch now holds an undecodable macro while a transfer is in flight (branch_in_flight, wired to the core's br_inflight), the redirect purges it, and a not-to-be-taken transfer still stops the machine. No check was weakened for this: the reserved-encoding runs still stop at their encodings and the ready cases still stop at their architectural ECALL. (2) The decoder's CI-format immediate read the destination register as the immediate, so c.addi x6,1 added 6. (3) A stale device attribute in the serializer, an inherited defect from the AMO lane that broke mmio.exactly_once. Sixteen cases were re-run green, and the suite from deleted build directories gives 51 of 53 passing, the two exceptions being a registered-but-unlanded case of another package (reconfigure.drain_and_generation, whose files do not exist yet) and mmio.exactly_once before defect (3) was fixed. CROSS-PACKAGE FINDING for p1, recorded rather than fixed: mepc still masks bits [1:0] because p0's config declares IALIGN=32 and the write mask is generated from it, so a trap taken on a 2-mod-4 compressed PC reads back rounded down. That is correct for p0 (C is a p1 capability) and the case asserts the trap *event* record instead; when C is enabled the generated mask and IALIGN must move to 16, which is a config change for the p1 profile rather than a defect in this package. NOT covered: a page boundary (no MMU in p0, so the harness's line is the only visible boundary), a cache-line refill (no L1I yet), a fetch fault as a synchronous trap (p0 stops instead), and most quadrant-1/2 ALU forms are decoded but not exercised end to end beyond the ones the case runs. ACT4 FOLLOW-UP (2026-10-01): the external suite found that c.lui placed its 6-bit immediate 16 bits too high (51 signature words against Sail) -- a defect compressed.cross_boundary could not catch because that case was written around the CI-format field position that had already failed (c.addi's), leaving the same format's other field unpinned. The decompressor is fixed and the suite passes that ELF; the mutant and the widened coverage are being added by the follow-up lane.

I-031.notes: The resource-ownership change FSM: IDLE -> STOP_ADMIT -> DRAIN -> ACK -> PUBLISH, with owner generations and idempotent control messages. Case PASS from a clean build: 4354 per-cycle shadow-exact comparisons over 4406 cycles (the RESULT line's 'checks' counter is the phase count; the substantive evidence is the per-cycle comparison against an independently represented shadow -- stacks rather than counters -- written from the contract). The card's rule is what is enforced rather than asserted: a new owner is published only after every outstanding uop, result and credit of the old owner has settled, and a repeated control message is idempotent. Six mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: PUBLISH_EARLY (a new owner published before the drain completes -- the card's first fail mode), NO_ACK (the drain treated as complete without the participant's acknowledgement), LOST_CREDIT, DOUBLE_CREDIT, REPEAT_CTRL (a non-idempotent control message) and DROP_ADMIT_AFTER_STOP. Ten other cases re-run green, including the corpus sweep, the memory cases and the arbiter. SCOPE, stated by the lane and recorded here: the FSM is standalone and is not yet instantiated by the fabric or the core -- that wiring is I-090/V-034's, and like the bypass (I-027), the steering policy (I-029) and the arbiter (I-030) it is verified in isolation until the fabric integration runs. NOT covered: p0 is single-hart so there is no second agent (the participants are modelled by the test's acknowledgement and the two event classes); the abort is a watchdog rather than a hang detector, so a credit settling after the abort leaves the next drain stalled as well; the 2^7 generation aliasing bound and the 8-bit message-sequence reuse bound are documented limits that no stimulus drives; the counters saturate at the architectural bound and no stimulus reaches saturation; there are no formal/SVA properties, only directed phases plus random shadow comparison; and the C++ shadow is the sole oracle, written by the same author though from the contract with an independent representation.

I-040.notes: LR/SC reservations, completing the A extension's implementation. Case PASS from a clean build: 73 checks. The reservation contract is DECLARED and checked rather than implied: the granule is the naturally aligned 64-byte block containing the LR address (GRANULE_BITS=6), verified as state against the address mask in every cycle a reservation stands (42 samples, 0 violations) and through its consequences (an in-granule store from the other agent breaks the reservation, an out-of-granule store does not). The card's forward-progress requirement is met the way it demands -- a declared bound, measured: N=16 attempts is compiled into the program as a hard ceiling with its own exit code, and the interfering run shows attempts == injected conflicts + 1, attempts <= N, with the case failing loudly if the stimulus injects >= N conflicting writes before any measurement. Four mutants each exit 1 with a precise first failure naming the ISA rule: SC_WRITES_ON_FAIL (the failing SC retires rd=0 where the ISA requires 1), SC_DOUBLE_WRITE (four write beats where two SCs succeeded -- 'exactly once' violated), NO_EXT_INVAL (three external writes clear nothing), and GRANULE_OVERINVALIDATE (an out-of-granule store breaks a reservation that must survive). Seventeen other cases were re-run green, including every memory and atomic case, the corpus sweep, the trap and retire verifications and the bring-up reference. NOT covered, stated by the lane: p0 is single-hart, so the second agent is the harness writing the shared memory model and raising an external-write notification, which is one event by construction -- the case therefore cannot distinguish invalidation-on-notification from invalidation-on-write, and there is no arbitration; a real multi-master test needs I-042/I-043/V-086. With no cache, any granule containing the LR address behaves identically, so the 64-byte size is not made *necessary* by anything this machine can do -- it is observable as declared state and through SC status, and that is the honest extent of it. aq/rl ordering effects are not demonstrated (the path is conservatively ordered; the bits are carried); speculative LR/SC is made unreachable by ROB-head serialization rather than tested; the misaligned LR/SC traps (cause 4 for LR, 6 for SC) are not exercised; atomic MMIO is neither claimed nor driven; a legitimate long retry cannot be exhibited because this implementation never fails spuriously; and no corpus program uses LR/SC. ACT4 FOLLOW-UP (2026-10-01): the external suite found the SC/reservation disagreement -- the DUT's SC succeeded where Sail expects failure, because the reservation granule was 64 bytes in both the RTL and its own case while the platform declares reservation_set_size_exp=3 (8 bytes). The case derived its addresses from the RTL's GRANULE_BITS constant, so it could not disagree with the design about the granule, and it never issued an SC at an address different from its LR -- the only observable the declared size controls. Both are being fixed: the granule comes from the platform declaration and the missing observable is added.

V-016.notes: PC transfer, fetch boundaries and FENCE.I visibility, compared per instruction against an ISA-derived expectation. Case PASS from a clean build: 93 checks over 6 runs, 85 retires, 805 cycles. Every situation the card names is produced with its specifics recorded: a JAL link value checked as a register value; two not-taken branches falling through to pc+4 and a taken branch reaching its target; a JALR whose computed target has bit 0 set (0x8000003D) cleared to 0x8000003C with the link at 0x80000034; positive and negative branch displacements across the 4 KiB page front (0x80000008 -> 0x80001004 and 0x80001008 -> 0x80000FD0); a 32-bit instruction at 0x80000FFE whose four bytes cross the harness's 8-byte line *and* the 4 KiB page front at 0x80001000 (line_straddles=2, page_straddles=1, and the event record still carries the instruction's own bits and a pc_after of +4); FENCE.I after a code patch with the patched word and its effect being what is fetched and executed; and a wrong-path fetch in which eight fetches faulted inside regions that were never executed, leaving no record, no stop, no refusal and no trap. Five controls: two harness-level (a PC masked to the line front; JALR's target served from the uncleared odd address) and three RTL mutants (FENCE.I not invalidating; a wrong-path undecodable macro leaking past the redirect; a branch-target mutant), of which the last was verified UNOBSERVABLE in the integrated core because the cluster recomputes the JALR target itself -- reported as a finding rather than counted as a control. Regression-checked here: the case passes and fence.code_and_data_order and core.corpus_branch pass after clean rebuilds. NOT covered, stated by the lane: 'page boundary' is only an address boundary because p0 has no MMU or cache; the integrated core produces no instruction-address-misaligned trap (only the bring-up core does), so a fault cannot be produced for a 2-mod-4 target -- an unaligned target is instead shown to execute, which is correct for C/IALIGN=16 but means the fault path is untested here; a fetch fault is a stop rather than a trap in p0; mepc on a 2-mod-4 PC is not exercised because the p0 CSR config declares IALIGN=32 (the same cross-package item I-041 raised for p1); there is no cache-line refill (no L1I), interrupts are tied off, the ISA reference implements only the RV64IM subset the six programs use, and there is no second-ISS differential.

I-032.notes: Bank-aware physical allocation, closing the fabric chain. Case PASS: 11 checks, 10195 shadow comparisons over 10275 cycles. Two new inputs (alloc_bias_en, alloc_bias_bank) make the allocation scan prefer the free tags of one bank and fall back to the full free set when that bank is empty, and acceptance still requires free_count >= need -- which is what makes the card's two fail modes impossible rather than merely untested: the bias cannot deadlock (a preference never removes a legal allocation), cannot leak a register and cannot steal one. The card's requirement that a gain be MEASURED rather than assumed is met: on 240 identical cycles with the bias off versus on, same-bank source-tag read-port conflicts fall 313 -> 259 with the accepted-allocation count, the stall count and the per-cycle free-count trajectory asserted identical, 75 preferred-bank hits and 53 fallbacks, and the bank histogram moving [31,55,42,0] -> [0,75,53,0]. The case asserts that the bias actually took effect, so a no-op policy cannot pass. Ten controls rebuild from deleted directories with their -D present, differ in hash and exit 1 naming the broken check: three new (BIAS_DEADLOCK, BIAS_UNRELEASED, BIAS_ARCH) and seven pre-existing ones in the edited regions, including the ten two-wide rules. The new stream also exposed and fixed a latent defect in the case's own random phase (a release aimed at a live identity after a tag recycle). NOT verified: the read-port delta is a same-bank source-tag proxy because the rename testbench does not instantiate the register file (prf.read_bank_collision owns that path), and the bias has no consumer in the p0 core, so its core-level effect is not measured; only p0 was built. CAVEAT recorded rather than smoothed over: the blast-radius core cases (both retire/commit head-block cases, core.trap_csr_program, core.mem_program, core.unwritten_reg_read, fabric.fixed_two_cluster, trap.precise_state, core.corpus_sweep, core.corpus_branch) were re-run and passed on the pre-final-cosmetic revision, but could not be re-run after it because a concurrent lane (I-044) left the core mid-edit and non-elaborating; the integration lead re-runs them once I-044 lands, and if any fails, this entry is amended rather than left standing.

I-049.notes: F/D implementation selected and packaged. The decision, written down before the code: SELF-IMPLEMENTED in rtl/core/mosaic_fpu.sv. No third-party FPU is vendored because this workstation has no network access, so no candidate could be fetched and its licence reviewed, and the only widely used reference (Berkeley SoftFloat, BSD-3-Clause) is C++ software -- an oracle, never a hardware datapath, which the card explicitly forbids as a substitute. Case PASS from a clean build: 19904 checks over 4735 operations in 56524 cycles (4735 accepted, 4733 completed, 2 cancelled by the case's own kill test), lint 42 sources clean. IMPLEMENTED, each with an independent oracle: fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv for both formats with all FIVE rounding modes (RNE, RTZ, RDN, RUP, RMM) and correct rounding; fsgnj/fsgnjn/fsgnjx; fmin/fmax; feq/flt/fle; fclass; fmv between integer and FP in both formats; fcvt in both directions including the RISC-V saturation rule and its NV flag; and fcvt.s.d / fcvt.d.s. DECLARED ABSENT rather than faked: fsqrt.s/d (which returns canonical qNaN plus NV -- a named marker, never a plausible number) and the fmadd family, both named so the list is not assumed complete by omission. The oracle is independent per operation class: arithmetic from the host's own FPU through fesetround/fetestexcept with volatile operands; integer conversions from the host's conversion; FP-to-integer (which has no C equivalent for the saturation rule) from a spec-written model cross-checked against the host in range; comparisons, fmin/fmax, fclass, fsgnj and fmv from bit-level ISA models; and RMM -- which this host cannot round -- from a directed tie table whose expectation is DERIVED from the host and whose every vector is PROVEN to be an exact tie by exact dyadic arithmetic, with a checked claim that binary division cannot produce a tie. The fflags contract is checked per operation (NV/DZ/OF/UF/NX). Latency is measured and compared against the unit's own declaration on every issue: one cycle for everything except fdiv, which measures 66 cycles and is shown operand-independent; a held result keeps value, flags and tag across the case's 100-cycle stall test. Four mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: RM_TIE_AWAY (a tie rounded away from the oracle), DROP_NX (NX omitted), NONCANONICAL_NAN, and FLUSH_SUBNORMAL (flush-to-zero where the policy is gradual underflow). The no-software-fallback rule is verified structurally rather than by grep: the unit has no memory interface, no instruction store, no control transfer and no architectural FP state, so there is nowhere for a software path to live. NOT covered: fsqrt and the fmadd family are absent, not implemented; RMM has no host oracle on this platform; subnormal coverage is of the rules rather than all 2^52 bit patterns; the comparison/fclass and FP-to-integer models are written in the driver and are the weakest link in the oracle story (the FP-to-integer one is at least cross-checked against the host in range); no synthesis, PnR, area or Fmax claim, because tools/synth_check.py is already blocked before this file by Yosys 0.69 and by a sibling's file; and there is no integration evidence -- decode/rename/commit of FP instructions is I-050/V-050, which this entry does not claim.

I-042.notes: Blocking L1 instruction and data caches. Case PASS from a clean build: 42 checks, trace equivalence between cache-on and cache-off, 167 cycles, with the observed activity recorded (data: 14 hits, 15 misses, 13 refills, 4 writebacks, 2 faults; instruction: 2 hits, 1 miss, 1 refill, 0 faults). Geometry is declared rather than implied: direct-mapped, 8 sets x 32-byte line = 256 bytes, 64-bit words, 32-bit addresses, 24-bit tags; the instruction cache is read-only and the data cache is write-back with write allocation. The card's two fail modes are the two things proven: a dirty eviction preserves every byte (dirty_eviction_preserved) and a faulted refill is never marked valid (fault_refill_invalid), each with its own mutant -- FAULT_VALID, DIRTY_DROP and WRONG_REFILL, all rebuilt from deleted build directories with their -D in the build command and exiting 1 with a named first failure. The valid-bit rule the card asks for is implemented as stated: valid bits are initialised without resetting the data RAM. NOT covered, stated by the lane: the non-blocking/MSHR path is deferred to I-043; coherence between the instruction and data caches after a store (self-modifying code, FENCE.I visibility) is not claimed -- self-modification within one data cache is exercised and V-016 owns the fence.i side; there is no PMA/cacheability input yet (that is I-039/I-093's address-source work); the memory port is line-wide one-beat; and the case is deterministic rather than a random soak. The caches are NOT integrated into the core: they are verified as modules, and wiring them into the fetch and memory paths is outstanding work, recorded here rather than implied. Second case, same task, and the one that makes the caches part of the MACHINE rather than modules beside it: cache.integrated_path passes at p1 (verified here from a clean build; 36 checks) with the instruction cache in the fetch path and the data cache in the memory path, cacheability from the generated platform map, MMIO and atomics bypassing the data cache, and an FENCE.I micro-FSM that flushes the data side, invalidates the instruction side and holds the front end off. THE EVIDENCE THAT THE CACHES ARE USED is the memory-port beat count falling from 4186 to 107 for the same program, with the architectural results identical on and off -- the card's 'a cache that never hits' silent-failure mode is what that number rules out. Four mutants each exit 1 with a recorded hash: FENCEI_NO_FLUSH (stale instruction bytes executed -- the card's own fail mode), DEVICE_CACHED (a device access reaching the cache), DIRTY_DROP and FAULT_VALID (reused from the module case, so the path is held to the rules its module already proved). ACT4 stays 127/127 and nineteen cases were re-run green across both profiles. THE PAYLOAD OBSERVATION FROM THE FIRST ATTEMPT IS RESOLVED, AND IT WAS NOT A DUT DEFECT: the driver's bus model accepted and queued fetch responses during the eight reset cycles (the fetch unit re-offers the reset-vector request while reset is asserted), and those seven queued responses -- all for address 0x80000000 with the same id and epoch -- were then consumed by the post-reset requests, because fetch matches a response to a slot by {id, epoch} and only a redirect advances the epoch. The word delivered for a given PC was therefore the word fetched earlier, which from outside looks exactly like a payload lagging its program counter. The lane proved the cause with an order-swap experiment (same RTL, same program, same reset: cache_en=1 first is exact, cache_en=0 shows the shift, so the anomaly follows the harness window and not the cache), fixed it in the driver only -- no RTL line changed -- and reduced it to a two-instruction reproduction that needs only that the first instruction after reset not redirect. The p0 corpus is immune by luck of its stimulus (its entry is a JAL, which bumps the epoch and drops the stale responses). HARNESS FINDING RECORDED FOR A FOLLOW-UP: tb_core_mem and the other core drivers accept bus traffic during reset the same way, so the hazard is latent in them; they do not exhibit it only because their programs happen to start with a redirecting instruction, which is a property of the stimulus rather than of the harness. A harness-wide rule (no bus traffic accepted while reset is asserted) would remove the class.  2026-10-02: the geometry is now config-driven from the profile's own caches block (MOSAIC_CACHE_LINE_BYTES, MOSAIC_L1I_SETS/WAYS, MOSAIC_L1D_SETS/WAYS, MOSAIC_MSHR_ENTRIES emitted by gen_manifest); p1 is 32 sets x 64 B x 4 ways = 8 KB per side, p0 keeps the historical 32 B/8-set/1-way stand-in. Lead re-ran cache.refill_evict_fault and cache.integrated_path: PASS.

V-017.notes: The CSR legality comparator: a machine-readable rule ledger with a positive and a negative example per rule, and a case that visits every rule and fails if any is unvisited. Case PASS from a clean build: 54 rules, 108 examples, 6493 comparisons over 3064 cycles, 769 retires, 22 traps. Deliverables: config/csr/rule_ledger.json (54 rules), config/schema/csr_rules.schema.json, ledger validation wired into tools/mosaic/config_check.py (so a malformed rule fails the config gate), a generated header build/<profile>/sim/mosaic_csr_rules.h, the driver sim/unit/tb_core_csr_rules.cpp and tools/run_csrrules_controls.py. Six controls each differ from the shipping binary and exit 1 with a named first failure, and they are exactly the card's three fail modes plus three RTL rules: SKIP_RULE (a rule silently unvisited), AUTO_WAIVER (a waiver generated from an observed difference instead of a declared rule -- the card's central prohibition), UNIMPL_ZERO (an unimplemented CSR accepted unconditionally as zero), CYCLE_WRITABLE, RO_WRITE_ACCEPTED and NO_FIELD_MASK. The 'reject the adjacent illegal result' requirement is what the example pairs encode: a strict rule's pair differs in one bit, and a WARL-allowed pair is paired with the adjacent pair that must be rejected. Gates green: lint 43 sources clean, slang-tidy exit 0, check_records, check_profile --all, make check, lint-cpp 57 files. NOT covered, stated by the lane: p0 is M-only so a permission error in the wrong mode is unreachable at runtime (the address-encoded minimum-privilege rule is checked structurally instead); mstatus.FS/VS early-dirty is not exercisable because p0 implements neither F/D nor V, so only the WARL encoding of both fields is tested and the precondition is recorded in the ledger; mip.MEIP reads zero (no PLIC) and is tested as read-only-zero; unimplemented CSRs are checked at three representative addresses rather than enumerated; counter values are pinned to ranges because they free-run; and mtvec vectored-entry arithmetic and misa's WARL extension bits are not re-derived here. RTL was read only, not edited.

I-044.notes: S/U privilege and PMP, delivered on the THIRD attempt (the first two are recorded in this file's blocked_tasks history and in the report; the defect that blocked them was D5, and the fix is the substance of this entry). Under --profile p1 -- the profile the card names -- the permission matrix passes with all 75 rows matching the ISA: checks=6300, 57 comparisons, 22623 cycles, 9296 retires, 52 traps. Under p0 it passes too (52 checks; p0 has no PMP entry, so those rows do not run there). THE FIX: a store's PMP check is now non-speculative and happens at ROB authorisation, which is the only place it can be both precise and non-speculative -- mosaic_pmp gained a store-commit query (two store-class lanes, W-only) and mosaic_core gates the retire request on the refusal and latches the system-trap staging register with EXC_STORE_ACCESS and tval = the access address. A refused store therefore never becomes visible, never retires as a success, and traps precisely with cause 7 at its own PC. The store queue's own source needed no change. Five controls each differ in hash and exit 1 with a named first failure, and one of them is D5 itself: STORE_DENY_NOT_TAKEN (shipping b57f1cbf64d8 exit 0; the mutant e9bb481e0f9b exits 1 at s-store-deny-w with mcause 9 where 7 is required), alongside LOCK_IGNORED, OVERLAP_INVERTED, M_MODE_ENFORCED and a driver-side FAULT_WRITES control for 'a permission fault still writes'. p0's PMP controls are inert and are recorded as inert rather than counted. FOUR defects were found and fixed across the three attempts (NAPOT comparing the free bits instead of the fixed ones, so an entry matched about one word of its region; a supervisor-CSR decode arm that never raised addr_impl; a read-only CSR encoding applied to reads; an illegal MRET/SRET executing before its exception), and this attempt found five more case/glue defects that the first-mismatch abort had been masking -- including THREE STANDALONE WRAPPERS that failed to elaborate because they never connected the endpoint's PMP ports, which means store.wrong_path_visibility, lsu.byte_forwarding and lsu.size_fault_boundaries were RED ON ARRIVAL from attempt 1 and are now repaired and re-verified here. Ten memory and core cases were re-run green. NOT covered, stated by the lane: the endpoint's post-retirement PMP check remains as a backstop; a lane-1 same-cycle store refusal is implemented but not exercised; AMO/LR/SC are unchanged; the M-mode 'last byte matches but first does not' divergence from attempt 2 is deliberately left untested and unchanged; interrupt-versus-store-refusal precedence is implemented but not observed; translation does not exist (I-045/I-046) and every address here is physical; satp is exercised only as a CSR and TVM/TW have no row of their own; no interrupt is ever asserted, so PMP at an interrupt boundary is untested. FOLLOW-UP CLOSED (2026-10-01): the exclusion ledger's EX-034 -- 'mepc[1:0] read-only zero (IALIGN=32 mask) while p1 claims the C extension' -- is fixed and the entry is marked covered. The alignment assumption now derives from the profile's claimed extensions rather than being a second hand-maintained flag, so a profile that claims C preserves mepc bit 1 and one that does not keeps IALIGN=32; the case grew an IALIGN probe phase that takes a trap on a 2-mod-4 PC and reads mepc back exactly (verified here: the p1 run passes with the ialign-odd-pc-mepc scenario observed, trap=1 cause=3), and a new mutant MOSAIC_CSR_MUTANT_MEPC_IALIGN32 (hash 18884fc15302 against the shipping 7e7d3e17b57c) exits 1 with the exact first failure 'mepc=0x80019100 expected 0x80019102'. The ledger is now 52 registered, 19 open / 33 covered, with check_exclusions and its 13 negative controls green. Ten cases were re-run green across both profiles. Two pre-existing p1-only failures were reported and are NOT in this path: lint_rtl --profile p1 fails on mosaic_pmp.sv's store_q0/store_q1 UNUSEDSIGNAL (p0, the required gate, is 45/45 clean) and csr.precise_trap_mret under p1 fails because the generated table row for sstatus has no known role (the case is registered and run at p0, where it passes). Both are dispatched as their own small package.

V-018.notes: Architectural memory separated from visible stores, with per-byte provenance. Case PASS: 1626 checks, 740 bytes carried a named producer, and ZERO wrong-path bytes leaked. The provenance rule is the deliverable: every byte that changed in memory had to name the committed store instruction that produced it -- identified by the machine's own identity rather than by PC, so two stores from the same PC in a loop are distinguishable -- and had to be the most recent committed store covering that byte at the time it appeared, checked against an independent model of architectural memory (never against the DUT's own view of what it wrote). Commit and drain are recorded separately, which is the card's title: no byte became visible before its commit. Coverage was asserted by the case: every load/store width, sign extension on loads, partial byte masks on stores, same-hart forwarding, a line-crossing access and a wrong-path store. ELEVEN controls, of which two are explicitly reported as UNOBSERVABLE through the integrated core and are not counted as evidence (SQ COMMIT_OUT_OF_ORDER -- the watermark is derived from the leading survivors, and LSU NO_SIGN_EXTEND -- the load queue extracts the value, so the endpoint's extraction is dead on this path): the observable ones include a wrong-path store's bytes made visible, a duplicated drain, a load returning a value no legal source could produce (stale data after a forwarded store was squashed), a driver control that drops the memory comparison and fails on a case the real comparison catches (the card's 'comparing only rd' fail mode), and store-size and branch-barrier mutants. Ten other cases were re-run green. CAVEAT recorded rather than smoothed over: this package verified against a PINNED committed revision (HEAD 3174a95, exported with git archive) because the live tree was mid-edit by the I-045/Sv39 lane at hand-off -- rtl/core/mosaic_core.sv fails to elaborate there (an unconnected req_tval_i) and every core case including this one is red on the live tree until that lane commits. The shipping binary hash (67f87996...) and the report's RTL hash table are that pinned revision. The integration lead re-runs this case on the final revision and amends this entry if anything differs. NOT covered, stated by the lane: I-036 speculative load replay and late-alias are NOT enabled, so the replay/rollback evidence the card asks for in that case is not claimed and the store-queue squash counter summed to zero over the run set; the MEM_VISIBLE record in the trace is emitted by the harness from the accepted data-port transaction rather than by a DUT-side producer, so schema reconciliation F-4 remains open; schema rob_id is left zero (a 14-bit field against the core's 16-bit lane id) with the lane identity travelling as an extra token; no trap is taken by the run set, so a faulting store's visibility and the trap path are not covered; the line-crossing coverage is a refusal rather than a split, because p0 traps a misaligned access before memory; no cache is in the core path, so 'a refill treated as a load effect' is not producible here. CAVEAT RESOLVED (re-run by the integration lead after the I-045 lane committed): the case PASSES on the final revision, not only on the pinned one -- `mem.visibility_provenance` passes from a deleted build directory on the tree where lint reports 44 sources clean and core.mem_program passes, so the 'verified at a pinned revision' qualifier no longer limits this entry. The pinned-revision numbers in the report remain as collected.

I-045.notes: The Sv39 page walker, verified both at its interface and INTEGRATED THROUGH THE CORE. Case PASS under --profile p1: 36 checks, with coverage asserted for all three levels as leaf and non-leaf, 2 MiB and 1 GiB superpages plus the misaligned superpage that must fault, a non-canonical address for load/store/fetch, V=0, the reserved W-and-not-R and bit-63 encodings, every permission bit in turn, SUM both ways, MXR both ways, page-table access faults (causes 1/5/7), every A/D situation, Bare mode, M privilege, an unsupported mode and a cancelled walk. The integrated half is what makes it more than a module test: S-mode is entered with mret and satp=Sv39, a translated load and store are observed as physical addresses on the data port with the PTE reads in level order, a non-canonical and a V=0 load trap with cause 13 and tval = the virtual address, no data-port transaction leaves RAM, and a store page fault is precise at commit (cause 15). THE A/D POLICY IS EXPLICIT, which the card demands: hardware update, not Svade -- a leaf with A=0 is updated, a leaf written by a store with D=0 is updated (A and D), each by an 8-byte compare-and-set PTE write that re-reads, compares and writes only if unchanged, with a mismatch re-evaluating; D is set only by a store; a refused PTE write is an access fault of the access class; and a walk cancelled before the write leaves no A/D update, which the case checks by reading the page table before and after. Five mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: ALLOW_NONCANONICAL (the card's first fail mode -- a non-canonical address reaching physical memory), PTE_ERROR_OK (the second -- a PTE error treated as a successful access), SUPERPAGE_UNALIGNED, SUM_IGNORED and AD_INVERTED. Seventeen cases were re-run green, including both profiles' memory, corpus, privilege and trap cases. NOT covered, stated by the lane: the TLB and SFENCE.VMA are I-046's, so every access re-walks and there is no stale-translation or ASID coverage (ASID is unimplemented and writes zero it); INSTRUCTION FETCH IS NOT TRANSLATED -- the integration is the data path only, and fetch-class semantics are covered at the walker interface with an identity-mapped S-mode stub, so a real S-mode fetch path is deferred to I-046/I-048; the I-042 caches remain module-level and are not in the access path; implicit PTE accesses are not checked against PMP (a PMA refusal of a PTE read is covered, a PMP refusal is not); the A/D compare-and-set is not atomic against a concurrent PTE writer, which is sufficient with one hart and one walk in flight but is a real limitation; and a store's translation is resolved at the commit boundary rather than at issue.

V-019.notes: An independent MMIO side-effect model. Case PASS from a clean build: 261 checks across eight scenarios, each with its own counts recorded (contract: 51 retires, 16 device accesses, 10 RAM, 8 effects; cancelled: 41 retires, 2 device, 3 RAM, 2 effects, 1 trap; and one scenario each for illegal width, unmapped read, unmodelled register, misaligned access, unmapped write and a write into the read-only test-harness window). The device model is the deliverable and it is deliberately awkward: destructive RX pops (a read changes state), idempotent STATUS/ID/MTIME reads, byte/halfword/word strobed SCRATCH writes, TX appends and a test-end write -- so 'each side effect happens exactly once with correct order and byte enables' is a real claim rather than a count of reads. THE CANCELLED SCENARIO IS THE CARD'S POINT and it passes: a wrong-path device read, write and pop behind a trapping ecall produce ZERO side effects while the wrong-path ordinary load still reaches memory (2 RAM transactions), which is what proves the window is real and not vacuous. Every error class is checked for the right cause AND the absence of a side effect: illegal width (cause 5), unmapped read (5), unmodelled register (5, and not silently zero -- the card's 'an unmodelled device defaulting to zero' fail mode), misaligned (4, with the device never seeing it), unmapped write (7 at dispatch) and a write into the read-only harness window (7). Fourteen controls were run, including driver-level ones that model the wrong contract (STATUS treated as scratch, a read-only register written) and RTL mutants from the device, store-queue and LSU paths; each exits 1 with a named first failure. NOT covered, stated by the lane: no interrupt is asserted, so the interrupt path around an in-flight device access (I-038's own stated gap) remains unmeasured; there is no device readiness handshake; mtime is a locked value rather than a counting timer; instruction fetch is not routed through the device model; only the p0 map is covered. FINDING recorded rather than fixed: the test-harness window's writability disagrees across config/memory/p0.json, the core's store map and the platform model -- three sources that should agree about whether that region accepts writes, and the disagreement is exactly the class of defect this project has hit before (a region whose permissions were only enforced in one place). It is recorded here for whoever owns the memory map next; the case pins the behaviour it observed rather than the behaviour it expected, and says so in the report.

I-046.notes: The TLB and SFENCE.VMA, the last gate on advertising Sv39. Case PASS under --profile p1 (33 comparisons; lint 45 sources clean). STRUCTURE, declared: mosaic_tlb.sv wraps mosaic_ptw -- 16 entries, 8 sets x 2 ways, set index va[15:13], round-robin replacement; the tag is the 4 KiB-granular VPN plus satp.ASID compared exactly, with a global bit so a G=1 leaf matches any ASID; it caches the translation, the leaf permissions and the A/D/G bits, re-evaluating permission on a hit with the SAME shared function the walker uses (so a cached permission decision cannot drift from a walked one); Bare and M bypass it; a store hits only if the cached D is set. Invalidation is generation-based -- every invalidation bumps a 16-bit generation and a walk installs only if its generation is still current, which is what makes 'a walk in flight at a fence cannot install a stale entry' a property rather than a hope. The SFENCE.VMA MATRIX IS TABULATED WITH WHAT EACH FORM ACTUALLY INVALIDATES, and the card's conservative direction is checked rather than assumed: all/all-ASIDs/globals for rs1=rs2=x0; that ASID only with different ASIDs and globals surviving for rs1=x0; the rs1 page across all ASIDs with globals for rs2=x0; that page in that ASID with other ASIDs and globals surviving for both; and a non-canonical rs1 invalidating nothing. A hit is PROVEN BY THE ABSENCE OF PTE READS on the memory port -- the only honest way to show a cache is used -- and the case also shows the negative the architecture permits: a PTE modification with no fence leaves the old translation in use. Five mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure and a recorded hash: SFENCE_NOOP (stale translation used -- the card's central failure), FENCE_WRONG_ADDR, CANCEL_IGNORED (an entry installed from a cancelled walk), SATP_NO_FLUSH and STORE_IGNORES_DIRTY. Fourteen cases were re-run green across both profiles. NOT covered, stated by the lane: instruction fetch is still NOT translated, so the TLB is on the data path only and 'shared between fetch and data' is not yet exercisable -- what exists is one instance on the one translation path that does, ready to be shared; single hart, so no cross-hart shootdown; the I-042 caches are still not in the access path; implicit PTE accesses are still not checked against PMP; a walk in flight at a fence is barred from installing but not terminated (a permitted behaviour, stated); the A/D compare-and-set is not truly atomic; and a store to a page whose cached D is clear re-walks until the walk sets D. ONE CASE-LEVEL NOTE recorded rather than fixed: core.trap_csr_program is a p0 case whose directed check hardcodes the p0 mstatus read-back (0x7eaa), so it fails under p1 on that constant -- a profile mismatch in that case's own expectation, not a translation regression, and it passes under p0. Whoever next touches that case should make the expectation profile-aware or register a p1 variant.

V-020.notes: No silent exclusions and no reference skips -- the package that decides whether this project's green lines mean anything, and the last gate on advertising the A extension. It records 52 exclusions (4 disabled checkers, 21 skips, 7 waivers, 15 unimplemented reference features, 3 timeouts, 2 generation failures), of which 32 are covered by a named alternative verification that exists AND passes, and 20 are OPEN with an end condition; the closure counts are printed rather than implied (4 checks disabled, 30 cases skipped, 14 fields waived). The checker is wired into make check, validates the ledger against its schema, verifies that every affected case exists in the registry, that every alternative-verification case exists AND has a recorded pass, and that every end condition is non-empty; a registered case with no recorded result that no ledger entry names is itself an unregistered exclusion. 13 negative controls are all rejected, each naming the offending entry -- including the card's central prohibition (a waiver generated from an observed difference) and a case filtered out of the total. The largest open exclusions it records, in its own words, are the most useful thing this package produced: (1) no ACT4 ELF executes for ANY advertised p1 extension -- A, C, Zicond, Zmmul, CMO -- because V-043 is undelivered, so those advertisements rest on this project's own cases rather than on an architectural test suite; (2) mepc[1:0] is read-only zero (the IALIGN=32 mask) while p1 claims the C extension, which is a genuine inconsistency in an advertised capability and is now tracked rather than forgotten; (3) no independent reference (NEMU, Sail or XiangShan) has ever been compared against this core -- every 'independent' expectation in this repository is a model written here; (4) four holes in the event interface (no MEM_VISIBLE producer, no interrupt event, three fields absent, store payload unwired); (5) p13's store-to-read-only trap has no independent oracle because only the DUT models boot_rom read-only; (6) one profile, one seed, and no device watchdog. Those six lines are the honest answer to 'what does this machine not prove yet', and they are machine-readable from here on.

V-043.verdict: PASS (127/127 after the five divergences were fixed; the failures are recorded above and in the report)
V-043.notes: The architectural test suite (ACT4) against the integrated out-of-order core. N IS CLOSED against the generation manifest, which is the card's central requirement: applicable=127, generated=127, run=127, passed=122, failed=5, with the ACT commit hash and the first failing ELF printed in the RESULT line (verified independently here: the case exits 1 for exactly those five). Coverage by extension: I 51, M 13, Zicsr 6, Zifencei 1, Zihpm 2, Zaamo 18, Zalrsc 4, Zca 32; the 47 excluded suites are each named with a reason in results/v043/suite_manifest.json, and the exclusions are recorded in the ledger rather than left implicit. The PASS macro is CALIBRATED rather than trusted: a corrupted expected-signature byte in I-add-00 makes the case exit 1, and MOSAIC_ALU_MUTANT_4 (slt unsigned) fails I-slt-00 -- so the suite can fail, which is what makes its passes mean anything. Ledger: EX-012 is narrowed rather than closed -- it now records the p1 ACT4 coverage and the five failures, names core.act_dut in affected_cases, and lists the extensions with no suite (Zicond) or no advertised implementation (Zmmul, Zicntr, Zicbom, Zicbop, CMO). NOTE ON THE TREE'S STATE: core.act_dut is registered and will report FAIL until the five divergences are fixed; that is the honest state and the suite is not to be narrowed or skipped to make it green. Gates green at the recorded revision: check_exclusions (52 registered, 19 open / 33 covered), check_profile --all, check_records. FOLLOW-UP (2026-10-01): THE FIVE DIVERGENCES ARE FIXED AND THE SUITE NOW PASSES 127/127 -- verified independently here from a deleted build directory (RESULT PASS core.act_dut applicable=127 generated=127 run=127 passed=127 failed=0, ACT commit 96493a91448ca50780013fd892daec2c204487ba). What each fix was, and what it says about our own cases: (1) c.lui placed its 6-bit immediate 16 bits too high -- compressed.cross_boundary could not catch it because that case was written around the CI-format field position that had already failed (c.addi's), leaving the same format's other field unpinned; fixed, with MOSAIC_DECODER_MUTANT_C_LUI_IMM as the control. I-043.notes: A non-blocking miss path with an MSHR. Case PASS from a clean build: 59 checks, 4 MSHR entries, and the observed activity recorded in the RESULT line (1 hit, 21 misses, 3 coalesced, 14 refills, 2 faults, 3 cancellations, 17 reads, max_outstanding=4 over 78 cycles). The card's requirements are the three things proven: duplicate misses to the same line are COALESCED rather than issued twice, a coalesced response is delivered to the right requester (identity, not arrival order), and a response that arrives for a CANCELLED request is not installed as valid and does not leave the MSHR occupied for ever. Three mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: NO_COALESCE (a duplicate miss issued twice), WRONG_ID (a coalesced response delivered to the wrong requester) and CANCEL_IGNORED (a cancelled request's response installed as valid). SCOPE, stated by the lane and recorded here: this is a READ-ONLY L1 path -- no store port, no write-allocate, no dirty bit, no writeback -- so the MSHR is not on the same cache that I-042 verified with a write-back data port; the two together are still not a complete L1. NOT covered: the shared return fabric and cross-cache coherence (this is a unit-level module with its own memory port, not wired into mosaic_core); PMA/cacheability decode, flush/invalidate, set associativity, victim buffers, ECC and a narrow/burst memory interface; the campaign is deterministic rather than a random soak. NO EXTERNAL SUITE COVERS IT: the p1 ACT4 configuration excludes caches, so the 127-ELF suite never routes through this L1 -- wiring it into the core's LSU endpoint is a precondition for that, and it is not done. The nine cross-package regression cases were deliberately NOT re-run: their source lists are provably disjoint from every file this package touches (verified programmatically), and the FP lane held mosaic_core.sv/mosaic_rename.sv/mosaic_dispatch.sv/mosaic_pkg.sv mid-edit, so a run then would have reported that lane's in-progress state rather than this package's effect. The integration lead re-runs them once the tree is green again. One registry fact: this package's arrival required adding rtl/core/mosaic_mshr.sv to I-042's rtl list as well, because both cases compile the same wrapper -- the third time this tree has paid for a case's source list being an elaboration dependency list rather than a list of the files it cares about.  2026-10-02: same config-driven geometry (4 MSHR entries from the profile); the non-blocking read path is wired into the core. Lead re-ran cache.mshr_nonblocking: PASS. A real coherence defect the larger L1 exposed (a bypassed AMO masked by a stale clean copy) was fixed with a targeted line-invalidate.

I-050.notes: FP rename/state and precise fflags commit, delivered on the third attempt. Case PASS from a clean build: 106 checks over 7 phases (verified here), and the external ACT4 suite stays 127/127 with it (verified here too). THE STATE DESIGN: rather than a second register file, the existing PRF's NAMESPACE was widened -- a parallel FP map family over the same 96-tag space, free list, generation table and undo journal, with 'an f-register never written' encoded as the x0 initial mapping (tag 0, gen 0) so it folds to ready-zero through dispatch's existing rule without pre-committing 32 extra tags, which would have violated the configuration checker's entry-count rule. THE FLAG RULE, which is the card's heart: the FP unit produces {NV,DZ,OF,UF,NX} with its speculative completion and never writes fcsr; the core records them against the ROB slot, clears the record at allocation and clears ALL records on rob_flush_pulse, and merges a slot's flags at retire only if the slot retires with the generation its record was written for. A squashed FP operation therefore contributes nothing, and the merge is ordered against a same-cycle csrw fcsr by ORing only lanes younger than that write. THE WRONG-PATH PHASE IS NON-VACUOUS, and building it produced a finding: the branch construction is IMPOSSIBLE in this machine, because dispatch's branch-in-flight barrier stops allocation for everything younger than an unresolved branch -- a mispredicted branch can only discard fetched-but-unallocated work (measured: the first stimulus had fp_issue=2, fp_flags=0). The phase is therefore built on a synchronous trap: an older divide delay, an older misaligned load that faults on its address, a younger fmul.s that completes with OF|NX, and a younger fdiv.s still in flight when the trap is taken -- and the shipping machine shows fp_issue=4, fp_commit=3, fp_flags=1, traps=1, wb_stale=0, fflags=0 and the destination register unwritten, which is the card's rule proven rather than asserted. The anti-vacuity check was kept and one more added (fp_issue >= fp_commit+1). FIVE controls, each rebuilt from a deleted build directory with its -D in the build command, a binary hash differing from the shipping one, and exit 1 with a named first failure: FFLAGS_EARLY (the card's fail mode -- architectural flags written when the FPU signals done), FP_SQUASH_WRITES (a squashed FP operation writing its destination), FP_NO_UNBOX, FP_NO_BOX (result NaN-boxing, added as a fifth) and FS_NO_DIRTY. Twelve cases were re-run green, including ACT4 (127/127), the corpus sweep, the privilege matrix and the translation cases. TWO REAL DEFECTS were found by the attempts and fixed: the frm CSR write took the operand's bits [7:5] (its place inside fcsr) instead of [2:0], so csrw frm silently did nothing -- a wrong rounding mode in the last bit of every result; and fp_s2_is_fp_c was never set for OP-FP, so dispatch resolved the second FP source through the INTEGER map and fadd.s f3,f1,f2 computed f1+x2. A third finding belongs to the CSR ledger rather than to FP: its stimulus used ld/sd displacements of 8*index, which overflow the signed 12-bit immediate past index 255, so the fflags example loaded from unwritten RAM and the hpmcounter rules had been passing vacuously -- fixed with two 256-entry windows and a permanent assembler displacement guard. NOT covered: fsqrt and the fmadd family are absent (I-049 declared them); frm is not renamed, so a dynamically-rounded operation younger than a pending frm write may use the old mode (the case makes its own frm ordering deterministic by indexing operands with the value the CSR read back); RMM is not driven because the host has no such mode; and NO EXTERNAL SUITE COVERS FP -- the p1 ACT4 configuration excludes F/D, so its 127 ELFs execute no FP instruction. Covering FP externally needs an F/D-enabled ACT4 configuration with a reference that executes F/D, or a dedicated FP conformance suite.

I-051.notes: The RVV descriptor and profile freeze -- the entry point of the vector chain. Case PASS from a clean build: 336 checks over 9284 enumerated combinations (2628 legal, 6588 illegal and rejected), 28 cycles, at VLEN=128 / ELEN=64 as the plan fixes them. The descriptor carries macro identity, an element bitmap and fault progress rather than one ROB entry per element, which is the card's rule and the reason vector work can exist in this machine at all: a 128-bit operation is one macro with a progress bitmap, not 16 uops fighting for ROB entries. Three mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure and a recorded hash: ILLEGAL_ACCEPTED (an illegal EEW/EMUL/SEW/overlap combination executing), LOSE_PROGRESS (a descriptor losing element progress, which would silently truncate a vector operation) and LANE_VLEN (a lane-count change altering the architectural VLEN -- the card's explicit fail mode, and the property the project's whole 'one hart keeps its architectural state across lane partitioning' claim rests on). The module is profile-independent: the same shipping binary hash was produced for p0 and p2, and the case passes under both. ACT4 was re-run and stays 127/127 (act_commit 96493a91...), and six memory/core cases were re-run green. SCOPE, stated by the lane: this is a module-level package -- the descriptor is NOT wired into the core or the LSU endpoint, and the vector datapaths (I-052..I-059) do not exist; deferred matrix rows are the vf4/vf8 extension ratios, segment (nf) and indexed address-group accesses, and fractional-LMUL field progress; vma/vta are not legality inputs; and only one descriptor exists (chaining is I-058). File hashes for the module, wrapper, driver and control runner are recorded in the report, as are the three mutant hashes. Second case, same task: rvv.vtype_layout passes from a clean build (1253 checks, 88 words and 88 descriptors round-tripped, 193 cycles, lint 50 sources clean). It fixes a SPECIFICATION-CONFORMANCE defect that the I-052 lane found in this package: the vtype field layout put vsew at bits 7:5 while the ratified RVV v1.0 format puts it at 5:3 ([2:0] vlmul, [5:3] vsew, [6] vta, [7] vma, [63] vill). A program reading vtype back -- which is how software discovers a machine's vector configuration -- would have decoded the wrong SEW. The fix moved the position in every artifact that encodes it (mosaic_vec_desc.sv, mosaic_vec_cfg.sv, config/csr/vector.json, the driver, and a control runner), and the lane SEARCHED for copies of the constant rather than fixing only the ones named to it: it found five independent copies of the old 7:5 layout across the descriptor, the configuration unit, the driver and the config's clause text, and confirmed there was no second wrong field position. It also resolved a disagreement between the table and the implementation rather than leaving it: config/csr/vector.json marked vtype access=rwr while the unit implemented the specification's URO rule, and the TABLE was wrong (an rwr description of what vset writes, not of what software may write) -- vtype is now access=ro with a zero write mask, matching vl and vlenb, and every profile's generated package was regenerated rather than hand-edited. Three mutants each exit 1 with a recorded hash and a named first failure: VTYPE_LEGACY_75 (the old layout back), VTYPE_SEW_WRONG (SEW decoded from the wrong bits) and VTYPE_SW_WRITE (software setting vill through a CSR write). ACT4 stays 127/127 and both existing vector cases pass on p0 and p2. Remaining and stated: vta/vma are stored and round-trip but the agnostic policies they select are not consumed (I-056+); there is no core integration (the units are driven through the vector testbench rather than a decoded vsetvli in the core, and the decoder's vtypei extraction was not touched); vsetivli's 11-bit vtypei interface width against the specification's 10 bits is a pre-existing detail left unchanged; and the descriptor's legality query does not itself test the reserved bits 62:8 because the configuration unit is the only producer of a vtype word -- adding a second copy of that rule is the duplicated constant this package removes.

I-047.notes: The SoC interconnect and error completion -- the first REAL device implementations, where the memory map, UART, timer and interrupt wiring had until now existed only inside testbench models. Case PASS from a clean build under p0 and p1: 48 checks, 187 cycles, with the RESULT line carrying the counts (accepted=15 normal=14 error=1 decerr=1 slverr=0, 4 device pops, 3 transmits, 1 exit). THE ACCEPTANCE RULE IS THE CONSERVATION IDENTITY and it is checked every cycle: every accepted request receives exactly one completion, normal or error -- which is precisely what the card's fail mode ('an AXI response error is dropped and the ROB waits for ever') looks like when it happens. THE ERROR MAPPING IS SPECIFIED rather than left to circumstance: an unmapped address produces DECERR (err=2) and involves no slave; a peripheral refusal -- a ROM write, a write into the read-only harness window, an unmodelled or misaligned device register, an AMO to a device -- produces SLVERR (err=1) with no side effect; both are delivered as the memory response's fault bit, which the LSU endpoint maps to a load access fault (5) or a store access fault (7) by the access's own write-enable. Four mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: DROP_ERROR (the card's fail mode), ID_SWAP (a response delivered to the wrong requester), STROBE_DROP (a narrow write losing its byte enables) and DUP_COMPLETE (a duplicated completion). Nine cases were re-run green, including the whole corpus sweep, MMIO exactly-once, the memory cases, and ACT4 which stays 127/127. SCOPE, stated by the lane: this is an additive module-level package -- rtl/soc/mosaic_soc.sv is a single self-contained module instantiated only by its own testbench, and it is NOT wired into the LSU endpoint or the core (that integration is separate work). It is a local bus with the properties the card requires (ID, strobes, backpressure, error completions) rather than a full AXI implementation: one outstanding transaction per slave, MAX_OUTSTANDING=4, no bursts and no separate channels. There is no PLIC (raw device interrupt lines only). The peripheral register map is V-019's, newly implemented in RTL, and the three existing device models are recorded as disagreeing rather than silently reconciled. mtime is a free-running counter with no timebase, write path or cross-domain synchronisation; the UART is a byte pipe without baud, framing or overrun; partial non-contiguous strobes are honoured but no core path drives them; there is no ECC or RAM collision matrix; and the campaign is directed rather than randomised.

I-052.notes: vsetvl/vsetvli/vsetivli and the vector CSRs. Case PASS from a clean build: 571 checks, 64 vtypes enumerated, 36 AVL bands, 276 cycles, and it passes under p0 and p2 with the same module. Four mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: AVL_UNCLAMPED (an AVL band choosing a vl beyond what the configuration permits), VILL_NO_BLOCK (vill failing to block execution -- the card's second fail mode), REPLAY_NEW_VTYPE (a replayed instruction using a newer vtype than its configuration snapshot, the card's first) and SILENT_M1 (an unsupported configuration silently becoming LMUL=1 rather than setting vill). ACT4 was re-run and stays 127/127, and rvv.descriptor_legality still passes. FINDING, recorded rather than papered over: the I-051 descriptor and config/csr/vector.json place vtype.vsew at bits 7:5, while the ratified RVV v1.0 vtype format puts it at 5:3. This package followed the family's recorded layout so that its descriptor snapshot stays consistent with the descriptor it feeds -- which is the right call inside one lane and the wrong answer for the machine, because a program that reads vtype back would see a different field position than the specification defines. The correction must move four artifacts together (mosaic_vec_desc.sv, tb_vec.cpp, config/csr/vector.json and mosaic_vec_cfg.sv) and is dispatched as its own package rather than left as a note. Other gaps stated by the lane: config/csr/vector.json marks vtype access=rwr (vset-written storage) while this unit implements the specification's URO rule for software writes; there is no core integration (module-level package, mstatus.VS is an input); no vstart-out-of-bounds trap (reserved, and the specification only recommends one); fault-only-first vl writes (I-056) and multi-macro snapshots (I-058) are out of scope. Environment note: build/p2/rtl/mosaic_csr_pkg.svh was 0 bytes during this run because a concurrent CSR change was mid-flight, so p2 lint failures on core/csr/interrupt/pmp at that moment are that change's, not this package's -- the vector files lint clean under both profiles.

I-048.verdict: PASS -- Stage A only; Stage B is an open exclusion, not a claim
I-048.notes: The p1 boot contract. STAGE A IS DELIVERED AND PASSES at p0 and p1 (verified here: 29 checks, and the RESULT line states which stage it ran and that Stage B has no artifact). It is a real boot chain: an M-mode firmware sets PMP, the trap vector and satp with a page table it builds itself, delegates what the profile allows, enters S-mode with mret, and runs an S-mode payload whose traps are all compared against ISA-derived expectations. The trap table, in the machine's own words: a load page fault on an invalid PTE (cause 13) to an S handler; a store page fault on a read-only page (cause 15) to an S handler; a load page fault on an execute-only page (cause 13) as the deliberate illegal access; a load access fault outside PMP (cause 5) to an S handler; an ecall from S (cause 9); an illegal instruction (mret in S, cause 2) to an S handler; a machine timer interrupt taken while in S to the M handler; an instruction access fault from S taken in M and then mret back to S (cause 1); a SUPERVISOR timer interrupt (STI) to an S handler; a supervisor software interrupt (SSI) to an S handler; and an sfence.vma after a mapping change, observed on the data port as the stale page faulting and the new page succeeding. That STI case exists because this package had to close a real gap: the interrupt controller had no STIP source at all (mip's writable mask had no bit 5), so a standard supervisor timer interrupt was unimplementable and the only path would have been delegating the machine timer, which is non-standard. The fix added STIP with its specification priority position and its software latch, and it forced the second real change: the delegation masks were narrowed to medeleg[9:0]/mideleg[1] at a time when page faults could not be delegated because translation did not exist and no supervisor timer existed. Both conditions are gone (I-045 is delivered), so the masks are now DERIVED from the profile's capabilities -- p1 has medeleg 0xB3FF (page-fault bits 12/13/15) and mideleg 0x22 (STI), while p0's generated package was diffed and is byte-identical, which is the right shape for a derived change. medeleg[11] (an ECALL from M-mode) is still never delegable, which is what the original narrowing was really protecting. Four controls each exit 1 with a recorded hash: NO_DELEGATION, SRET_NO_RESTORE, BAD_PAGETABLE and BANNER_ACCEPTS (a driver control that would accept a Linux banner as success, shown to fail the real self-check -- the card's own fail mode made into a control). ACT4 stays 127/127 and fourteen cases were re-run green, including both profiles of the interrupt and privilege cases (interrupt.boundary_replay's expectation was made profile-aware rather than left hardcoded to p0's mip shape). STAGE B IS NOT CLAIMED: no firmware image, DTB, kernel or rootfs exists anywhere in this environment, and open exclusion EX-053 names all four, the hash each would need, and the end condition. Also recorded rather than claimed: an observation that a software interrupt taken at a one-instruction self-loop immediately after the csrw sip that raised it left the core in `recovering` without progress (naming the first post-write instruction as the interrupted PC avoids it) -- that is a potential machine defect for a follow-up package, not a property of this one. Other gaps stated: no Sstc/stimecmp (STIP is platform/software-driven, the standard non-Sstc path); instruction fetch is still untranslated, so S-mode code is identity-mapped and a fetch page fault cannot be taken; mtval for a system illegal-instruction trap is 0 (exclusion EX-046).

I-053.notes: The banked vector register file and its lane mapping -- the structure the whole vector story depends on, and the one the plan insists must not change a hart's architectural state when the number of physical lanes changes. Case PASS from a clean build: 3806 per-cycle comparisons over 3846 cycles, and the RESULT line states the two properties that matter: read latency is 1 cycle, and LANE COUNTS 2, 4 AND 8 READ THE SAME LOGICAL VECTOR. THE MAPPING IS A DECLARED RULE, not an emergent one: geometry VLEN=128, ELEN=64, 32 registers, BANK_W=32, 32 banks, 4 rows, with row = r/8 and bank = (r%8)*4 + word; the element-to-group address is computed from SEW and LMUL (grp_bits = VLEN<<LMUL for LMUL>=0, VLEN>>-LMUL for LMUL<0, phys = (base & ~(grp_regs-1)) + bit_off/VLEN); SEW<=32 fits in one bank word and SEW=64 spans two; elements outside the group are refused and counted. The port structure is stated too -- a read bank serves RD_PORTS distinct rows and broadcasts a shared (bank,row), a write bank serves WR_PORTS rows with no sharing, and refused demands are retried and counted (backpressure rather than loss). THE LIFETIME RULE is the subtle one the card asks for: a write is REFUSED while its bit range overlaps a read that has been granted but not yet presented, so a destination aliasing a source or the mask can never overwrite an element that has not been read -- which is the vector equivalent of the store queue's ordering discipline. Four mutants each exit 1 with a recorded hash and a named first failure: LANE_PERMUTE (the mapping permuting elements when the lane count changes -- the card's first fail mode), LOSE_ELEMENT, PLATFORM_LATENCY (read latency varying with the platform, the card's second fail mode) and OVERLAP_CLOBBER (a write granted over an unread element). SCOPE, stated by the lane: module-level only, not wired into the core (that is I-054 and the fabric integration); the geometry is fixed at p2 and read latency measured at 1; storage is not reset (the driver primes every word first); the lifetime guard is exact at element granularity but conservative across mixed widths; the lane quota is a runtime input rather than three parametrised instances, which is the honest way to have tested 2/4/8 in one build; and the campaign covers four seeds.

I-090.verdict: PASS -- and this is the package that supplies the goal's measured dynamic-versus-fixed comparison
I-090.notes: The fabric integration: the modules this project built and verified in isolation are now part of the live core, and the dynamic-versus-fixed comparison is MEASURED rather than inherited. WIRED IN: the bank-aware allocation (I-032, with the preferred bank driven from the routing decision), the local bypass (I-027, instantiated in the cluster with its registered slot exposed as an earlier value-visible wakeup feeding a new second wakeup port on the issue queue), and the steering policy (I-029, replacing the alternating toggle for every cluster-bound macro while the fixed baseline remains selectable through the same single-bit input). LEFT OUT, with reasons: the bounded-service arbiter (I-030), because its request/queue model does not compose with the writeback arbiter's per-producer pending registers and its write/rename/ROB completion decision -- inserting it is a redesign of the durable completion path rather than a wiring change -- and the ownership FSM (I-031), because it exists for reconfiguration, which p0 and p1 never perform, so wiring it in would be dead logic (the card explicitly allows leaving it out, and adding dead logic to a machine whose counters and valids are the evidence would be worse than leaving it). THE MEASUREMENT, on equal resources: the same ELF (p02_branch.i0), the same seed, one toggle. Architectural results IDENTICAL -- 71123 retired events, the whole retire stream and all four signature words equal field for field, with the physical destination id deliberately excluded as non-architectural. Measured difference: 448406 cycles fixed against 448468 dynamic, i.e. the dynamic configuration is 62 cycles (0.014%) SLOWER on this program; the cluster balance moves from 214/17624 to 8498/9340 integer-ALU issues and from 17767/17769 to 18790/16746 branch issues, the router grants 57281 (reason histogram load=14, age=57267), and the bypass captures 17849 with 33 early-resolved operands. The per-step table (tools/run_fabric_steps.py) isolates each contribution: steering alone is cycle-neutral while balancing, the bank preference costs about 80 cycles, the bypass recovers about 18, and a bypass-only run with fixed affinity shows 2 captures. THE SLOWDOWN IS REPORTED AS A FINDING, not hidden -- a steering policy that helps on one program and hurts on another is exactly what the plan's 'measured, not inherited' requirement exists to expose. Three controls each exit 1 with a named first failure: IGNORE_CAPABILITY (steering sends an ALU macro to the LSU, where it is executed as a memory access and the dynamic run hits its cycle bound), DYN_SWAP_SRC (the dynamic route's operand-value wires cross, so the run exits after 72 instructions with a different signature -- the fail mode that matters most, since dynamic scheduling must never change what the program computes) and NO_DELTA (the strategy input held low, so the 'dynamic' run is the fixed machine and no measurable difference exists -- a control on the MEASUREMENT, so the comparison itself is falsifiable). ACT4 stays 127/127, eighteen cases were re-run green including both profiles' privilege, translation and boot cases, and every gate is green (make check, both profiles' lint 51/51, slang, lint-cpp 68 files, check_records, check_exclusions and its negative controls). Registry note: the lane added mosaic_steering.sv and mosaic_cluster_bypass.sv to the source lists of the 26 cases that build the core -- a mechanical dependency following the rule that a case's rtl list is its elaboration dependency set; no task, status or pending field was touched.

I-054.notes: The vector integer datapath: 99952 checks over 346 family/width/LMUL cells and 106824 cycles, verified here from a clean build. SEVENTEEN FAMILIES ARE IMPLEMENTED and each is named in the report: add/sub (including vsub reversed), the widening forms, multiply and its high-half variants, the widening multiply, shifts, the narrowing and clipping forms, logic, min/max, the comparisons, the SATURATING arithmetic (vsadd/vssub/vaadd/vasub and their unsigned forms), the mask logic, the mask prefix operations, slides, gather, compress, the reductions and the widening reductions. SEVENTEEN ARE DECLARED ABSENT with names -- integer divide and remainder, the multiply-accumulate family, the scaling shifts, the fractional multiply, the integer extensions, viota/vid, vrgatherei16, the merge and move forms, vector AMO, vector memory (I-056) and vector floating point (I-055) -- and because no capability bit exists for them they cannot be advertised, which is the card's fail mode ('implementing only vadd/vmul and declaring V complete') made structurally impossible rather than merely avoided. THE REDUCTION ORDERING IS STATED ONCE and checked two ways: a reduction folds source elements in strictly ascending element index order from vstart, over active elements only, with vs1[0] as the initial accumulator, with no tree, no reassociation and no parked partial accumulator (and vwredsum collecting into a 2*SEW accumulator); the case compares the running accumulator against the specification's left-to-right fold at every step AND requires the engine's element trace to be exactly vstart..vl-1 -- which matters because integer addition is associative, so the sequence is the only observable of the order and it is also what a vstart restart must reproduce. MASKED-OFF ELEMENTS MAKE NO ACCESS: the mutant that lets one through is caught by name, and the case drives a would-fault index with the mask clearing it and requires neither trap nor memory traffic. Five mutants each exit 1 with a recorded hash and a named first failure: SAT_WRAP (saturation wrapping instead of clamping, caught at the signed boundary), WIDE_WIDTH (a widening operation reading the wrong element width), PERMUTE_ORDER, MASKED_ACCESS and REDUCE_ORDER. ACT4 stays 127/127. SCOPE, stated by the lane: the vector unit is NOT wired into the core (no decoded vector instruction reaches it and the descriptor's element bitmap/fault progress is not bound to the engine -- the partial-trap restart is I-057); vstart restart is implemented as a gate but no phase drives it, and the mask-prefix operations do not raise on a non-zero vstart (I-057); LMUL=8 is out of scope for the widening and narrowing families because the effective LMUL would be 16, outside the [1/8, 8] the descriptor admits -- the unit refuses it and the cell is excluded from the 346 rather than silently skipped, which is the right way to handle an out-of-range cell but means the count is 346 of what would otherwise be more. Finally, two gate failures at the time of writing belong to the cache lane's in-flight files, not to this package: lint-slang flags mosaic_core.sv using cache_fence_busy before its declaration, and lint-cpp flags missing wrapper ports in the cache driver; both files of this package are individually clean under the same tools. SECOND CASE, SAME TASK, closing the conformance question the vstart fix flagged: the three mask prefix operations had two of them sharing one expression. THE RULES, established from the specification (v-spec adoc at the pinned revision) rather than from the RTL, with k the first set bit over the active elements and pfx the OR of source bits strictly before i: vmsbf[i] = ~(pfx|bit_i) -- set strictly before the first set bit; vmsif[i] = ~pfx -- set up to and including it; vmsof[i] = bit_i & ~pfx -- only that bit. THE DEGENERATE CASES ARE WHERE THE OPERATIONS DIFFER, and the case states them explicitly because they are counterintuitive: for an ALL-ZERO active slice vmsbf and vmsif are all-ONES while vmsof is all-zeroes -- the three are NOT symmetric, which is exactly the kind of thing a reader would guess wrong -- and for a first set bit at position 0 vmsbf is all-zeroes while vmsif and vmsof set bit 0. THE DEFECT: vmsbf was implemented as ~pfx, which is vmsif's expression, so it set bit 0 as well and was wrong for any source with a set bit; fixed to ~(pfx|bit_i). The case passes from a clean build (verified here): 1115 checks, 3 operations, all 16 first-set-bit positions, 3 all-zero cases and 9 SPEC-ANCHOR cells that use the specification's printed examples rather than the host oracle -- which is what makes the oracle's independence checkable in turn. Three mutants each exit 1 with a recorded hash: MASKPFX_SAME_EXPR (the two expressions identical again, i.e. the defect as found), MASKPFX_ALLZERO (the all-zero slice cleared instead of set) and MASKPFX_POS0 (a bit set before k=0), and the three mutants of the vstart case were re-verified 3/3. A SECOND, PREVIOUSLY INVISIBLE DEFECT WAS FOUND BY BEING THE SECOND READER, which is the point of this package: the packet engine's mask-DESTINATION write element was (cur_q>>3)<<3, so every mask-destination element at or above 8 wrote byte 8 while the read path used cur_q>>3, leaving destination bytes stale -- invisible because no existing packet mask case drove vl above 8, and exposed the moment this case drove positions 8 to 15. Fixed to match the read path. The mask-logic neighbours (vmand, vmnand, vmor, vmnor, vmxor, vmxnor, vmandn, vmorn) were checked against the specification and match exactly, including operand order; vmerge and the move forms are not implemented and carry no capability bit. ACT4 stays 127/127 and thirteen cases were re-run green. NOT covered, stated by the lane: masked mask-prefix sources (where the search runs over ACTIVE elements only); the destination-agnostic setting on a masked-off mask destination; CORE-LEVEL illegal-instruction routing for the mask-prefix vstart rule (the vector unit raises it and the core has the path, but no case drives it at core level -- recorded rather than assumed); register-overlap legality (vd against vs2, vd against v0); and only SEW=8 at LMUL=1, i.e. the 16-bit mask range, is driven. THIRD CASE, SAME TASK, closing the masked forms the semantics package named as unproven -- and the honest outcome is that THE RTL WAS ALREADY CORRECT: the search for the first set bit runs over ACTIVE elements only (the packet engine updates its running prefix only when the element is active, and a masked-off element takes the execute path with no source read at all), so no value-path fix was needed and the deliverable is the coverage that proves it plus the controls. THE RULES, established from the specification with its printed masked examples as anchors: for vmsbf.m/vmsif.m/vmsof.m with a mask operand, k is the first set bit over the active elements only; a MASKED-OFF source element contributes NOTHING to the search (it is ignored rather than read as zero, which is the distinction a search-over-all-elements implementation gets wrong); for every active i, vmsbf sets i<k, vmsif sets i<=k and vmsof sets only i==k, with the all-ones or all-zeroes result when no k exists; and a masked-off mask destination or a tail element follows vma/vta -- undisturbed for 0, the mask-agnostic all-ones for 1. The case passes from a clean build (verified here): 2870 checks over 168 cells -- 48 first-active-position cells, 45 where a masked-off set bit precedes an active one (the configuration where the two searches DISAGREE, which is why it is the largest single group), 48 where the only set bit is masked off, 12 vma cells, 12 vta cells and 3 spec-anchor cells using the specification's own printed examples -- deterministic across seeds 1/2/7/12345 and passing under p0 and p1. Three mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: MASKPFX_SEARCH_ALL (searching over all elements instead of the active ones), MASKPFX_MASKED_SRC (getting a masked-off element's contribution wrong) and MASKPFX_VMA (the destination-agnostic behaviour on a masked mask destination). ACT4 stays 127/127 and all the named vector cases pass. A REAL GAP IS RECORDED RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLICIT: the core's vector ALU lane is instantiated with the ADDSUB and LOGIC capability bits only, so MASKPFX IS NOT ADVERTISED and the core refuses these operations -- the unit supports them and the core will not dispatch them, which is the kind of mismatch between what is verified and what the machine advertises that the capability ladder exists to catch. NOT covered, stated by the lane: that core-level routing (recorded above); the single-element lane's prefix output is not gated on activity in a way the unit can observe; vl below 16 with masked-off elements below vl; and the masked form with a non-zero vstart, which the vstart package owns because its gate is mask-independent. One environment note: lint-cpp was red at the time only on the sibling locality lane's in-flight driver file, and this package's own driver syntax-checks clean. 2026-10-02: the core now ADVERTISES the mask families it had only implemented -- the gap this project's own record named as 'the unit supports what the machine will not dispatch'. Two gates were closed, not one: the capability word gained MASKLOG (bit 10) and MASKPFX (bit 11) (VEC_ALU_CAPS = 17'b0001100_0100_0001, ADDSUB + LOGIC + MASKLOG + MASKPFX), and the core's vector decode had NO OPMVV arm at all, so an OPMVV arm was added (funct6 010100 with rs1 selecting the mask-prefix operation, funct6 011000..011111 with vm=1 selecting the mask-logical family) -- the capability word alone would not have made the operations decodable. MASKPFX is justified by rvv.integer_mask_permute plus rvv.mask_prefix_semantics (1115 checks), _masked (2870 checks including 45 masked-off-before-active cells) and _vstart (79 checks); MASKLOG is justified by reading rvv.integer_mask_permute's PhaseMaskLane stimulus, which drives all eight MASKLOG ops against the host oracle -- read, not inferred from the case name. New case vec.mask_prefix_at_core (registered for this package, 112 checks, 4 phases: plain, masked, masklog, vstart) PASSES at p0 and p1 under the lead's own run: RESULT PASS vec.mask_prefix_at_core checks=112 phases=4 plain_cycles=7723 masked_cycles=27063 masklog_cycles=5287 vstart_cycles=446. The vstart rule is tested at the core level: an illegal vector instruction with vstart=2 traps with mcause=2 at its own PC, mtval=0, the destination mask register unchanged, vec_fault=0, and the vstart CSR left unmodified -- the V-spec illegal-instruction rule -- and no core-versus-unit disagreement was found. Two controls, each from a deleted build directory with a binary hash distinct from the shipping one and exit 1 with a named first failure: MOSAIC_CORE_MUTANT_VEC_CAPS_NO_MASKPFX (clears bit 11; 'prefix-plain: no trap is taken') and MOSAIC_CORE_MUTANT_VEC_ILLEGAL_AS_FAULT (reports the refusal as a resumable element fault instead of an illegal instruction; 'vstart: the refusal is an illegal instruction (mcause=2), got 5').
