I-056.notes: The vector memory packetizer. Case PASS from a clean build: 2350 checks over 8 modes and 61 cells in 3893 cycles (verified here; lint 55 sources clean). EVERY MODE THE CARD NAMES IS IMPLEMENTED and the lane's own 'absent' list is EMPTY: unit-stride, constant-stride, both indexed forms (ordered and unordered), the three segmented forms (unit, strided and indexed), the whole-register loads and stores for NFIELDS 1/2/4/8, and the mask load/store. That completeness matters because the card's fail mode is 'a segment or whole-register mode left unimplemented while V is advertised' -- a machine that implements only the easy modes and advertises V is the classic vector shortcut, and this record can say it does not apply. THE FAULT RULE IS ELEMENT-GRANULAR, which is the substance of the package: items are issued in ascending logical order, and on a fault the macro stops with o_trap_elem_o = the faulting element index -- which is exactly the value a vstart restart needs -- with no item at or after the fault issued, a store at or after it not performed, a load's destination at or after it untouched, and the elements strictly before it having taken effect with their queued responses drained. A whole-macro trap, or a vstart of zero for a fault at element k, is rejected by the case rather than accepted. Ordered-indexed ordering is enforced and checked (element i completes before i+1 is issued). Four mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: MERGE_CROSS_REGION (a line merge crossing a permission boundary -- the card's first fail mode), WHOLE_FAULT (a macro-granular fault instead of the element's), MASK_WRONG (a byte mask wrong for its width and position) and ORDERED_REORDER. ACT4 stays 127/127. NOT covered, stated by the lane: the unit is not wired into the core (no decoded vector memory instruction reaches it); there is no TLB/PMP/PMA in this path (the memory port supplies the fault); misaligned elements that would leave the 8-byte beat are not implemented; vector AMO and fault-only-first are absent and unadvertised; the vstart restart is not re-executed (I-057); segment NFIELDS 3/5/6/7/8 and the ordered indexed-segment form are implemented but not covered by the case; unordered stores are issued strictly by design; and throughput is out of scope.

I-057.notes: Vector partial trap, vstart and fault-only-first. Case PASS from a clean build: 613 checks over 48 fault cells, 6 interrupt cases, 12 fault-only-first cases and 3 restarts in 2859 cycles (verified here). THE STORE SIDE-EFFECT RULE IS PROVEN BY COUNTING BYTES, not by argument: on a fault at element k the packetizer has performed elements < k (stores applied, loads written back) and withheld element k; the controller commits [0,k) into the descriptor bitmap and publishes the restart point as the bitmap's first clear bit, so the re-execution begins at k and a store that already wrote 0..k-1 is not written again. The case counts memory writes PER BYTE across the fault, the restart and the completion and requires every byte written exactly once, with the two-run request stream exactly 0..k then k..vl-1 (the faulting element is re-issued because its store was withheld) -- which is precisely the card's 'a restart must not duplicate an irreversible side effect'. Five mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: WHOLE_TRAP (a whole-macro trap where the specification requires a partial one -- the card's first fail mode), REDO_COMMITTED (a restart re-performing an already-committed element), FOF_TRAPS (a fault-only-first load raising a trap instead of absorbing), VSTART_OFF_BY_ONE and EARLY_RETIRE (retiring when only the last packet arrived -- the card's second fail mode). A CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF, recorded because it is the right way round: I wrote that fault-only-first should shorten vl 'in both' the first-element and later-element fault cases. The lane checked the specification, found that element 0 of a fault-only-first load TAKES A TRAP with vl UNMODIFIED while an element k>0 is absorbed with vl reduced to k, cited the pinned tag and line numbers for it, confirmed it against the ratified manual, and implemented the specification rather than the brief. The brief was wrong and the record says so. Other rules stated: only page and access faults are absorbable, an interrupt is never absorbed, and a strided form or a store is never absorbed; destination elements at and after the fault are left untouched so a re-execution re-loads nothing that already succeeded. ACT4 stays 127/127 and the sibling vector cases all pass. NOT covered, stated by the lane: the vector unit is still not wired into the core (no decoded instruction reaches the controller); interrupts at an element boundary are implemented as a unit handshake only (core-level delivery, epc and mcause are not in this package); the vstart restart for the arithmetic path is not exercised here; the mask-prefix operations with a non-zero vstart must raise illegal-instruction per the specification and neither this package nor I-054 implements that rule (reported by both lanes, now recorded rather than lost); only unit and strided forms are swept for boundaries; and the fault class is carried rather than decoded (no TLB/PMP/PMA in this path). SECOND CASE, SAME TASK, closing a conformance gap that TWO lanes reported independently: the RVV specification requires vmsbf/vmsif/vmsof with a non-zero vstart to raise an ILLEGAL-INSTRUCTION exception, because a prefix mask operation cannot be resumed mid-way. Case PASS from a clean build (79 checks over the three operations and six vstart cells in 394 cycles, verified here). The rule is implemented as ONE whole-instruction predicate (the family is MASKPFX and vstart is non-zero) that drives both the boundary element lane's illegal output and the packet engine's setup refusal -- the engine moves straight to done before any element step -- so the refused instruction reads no source, writes no destination, changes no destination byte, and is reported as an ILLEGAL INSTRUCTION rather than as an element fault, which matters because the two take different architectural paths. vstart=0 still executes normally. Three mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: MASKPFX_NO_TRAP (no exception at all), MASKPFX_TRAP_VSTART0 (trapping even at zero) and MASKPFX_WRONG_OP (trapping for the wrong one of the three). A SECOND SEMANTIC QUESTION WAS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN rather than guessed at, and it is worth carrying: the element lane gives vmsbf and vmsif the same result expression, whereas the specification distinguishes them at the first set bit (vmsbf sets the bits BEFORE the first set bit, vmsif sets them up to and including it). The lane flagged it as out of scope for a vstart fix rather than changing arithmetic it was not asked to touch -- which is the right call -- so it is recorded here as an open correctness question, with the note that rvv.integer_mask_permute's mask-value semantics are the package that owns it. Also not covered: vstart >= VLMAX, and the core-level illegal-instruction routing (this case is at the unit level). ACT4 and vec.integrated were not re-run by this lane because the concurrent I-059 lane was editing the core; the integration lead re-runs them in the consolidated pass -- and note that the change is vector-unit-only, so a scalar suite cannot be affected by it. THIRD CASE, SAME TASK, settling a defect the COALESCING lane had recorded rather than patched. VERDICT: the finding was REAL for exactly one stop kind and is fixed; the others were already correct and are now PROVEN BY CONSTRUCTION per kind. The four kinds and their rules, established from the specification and this package's own contract before anything was changed: (1) an ELEMENT FAULT at k with vstart=k -- the elements before k have committed and their in-flight responses must be written back, while the elements at and after k are re-executed and their responses discarded, which was already correct because responses are in order; (2) a WHOLE-MACRO TRAP (reachable as a fault at element 0 and as the coalesced-group fallback from I-061) -- every element is re-executed, so all in-flight responses are discarded, correct; (3) a REDIRECT/CANCEL, which on this unit is the precise-interrupt boundary stop at b -- everything below b has committed so every in-flight response must be written back, and NOTHING is issued at or after b -- and this is THE DEFECT: the abort signal gated the writeback push, so an in-flight load whose element had already committed was dropped and that element was lost for ever; (4) the LANE BROKER's drain (I-059), which is not a packetizer stop at all -- the broker waits for the macro to become idle -- so the macro completes and every response is written back, correct. The case passes from a clean build (verified here): 63 checks over 4 stop kinds, 7 cells, 5 restarts and 3 in-flight positions. THREE mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: STOP_DISCARD (re-injecting the reported defect), STOP_WRITEBACK (the MIRROR error -- writing back an element that will be re-executed, which leaves a stale value a later restart overwrites, the kind of defect that surfaces much later as a wrong result) and STOP_REISSUE (the boundary naming the element before the first not-performed, so the resume re-issues a completed element and duplicates a store write). THE LANE THAT REPORTED THE PROBE NOW HAS IT AS A PERMANENT CHECK: coalesce.element_faults with STOP_DISCARD exits 1, so the coalescing package's temporary probe became a regression test rather than a transcript entry -- which is what the project wants to happen to every finding. ACT4 stays 127/127, the case passes at seeds 1/2/7/12345 and profiles p0 and p2, and the ten protected vector cases plus the three control suites (I-056 4/4, I-061 4/4, I-057 5/5) all pass. NOT covered, stated honestly by the lane: NO REDIRECT/CANCEL INPUT EXISTS on this unit, so a true pipeline squash is unreachable -- and the abort-only path would write back, which would be WRONG for a squash, so the header says so rather than leaving a latent trap for whoever wires a squash in; the lane broker is not instantiated in the vector testbench, so its row is the property the drain relies on rather than the broker protocol itself; stores are issued strictly so no store response is ever in flight at a boundary stop, meaning the store rows carry the resume and no-duplicate-side-effect half only; only unit-stride macros are driven with a stop; the fault response is held for a fixed number of cycles to make the later element's flight deterministic rather than a race; and the specification's permission to update elements past vstart is deliberately not taken, in favour of the stronger 'unperformed' statement.

I-055.notes: Vector floating point with per-element exception flags. Case PASS from a clean build: 13828 checks over 10 families and 25 cells in 80930 cycles (verified here; lint 57 sources clean). IMPLEMENTED: element-wise add/sub/reversed-sub/mul/div/reversed-div in both register and scalar form at SEW 32 and 64, min/max, the sign-injection group, the six comparisons with a mask destination, the element-wise conversions, the widening and narrowing conversions (including the rtz forms), the ordered and unordered reductions, the min/max reductions and the widening ordered/unordered reductions. ABSENT WITH REASONS AND NO CAPABILITY BIT: vfsqrt (the scalar square root is absent per I-049), the whole fused multiply-accumulate family (the scalar fmadd is absent per I-049), vfncvt with round-to-odd (not one of the shared FPU's five modes), the merge and move forms, the widening arithmetic, and half precision (the F/D datapath has no half format, so SEW=16 is refused). THE FLAG RULE AS IMPLEMENTED: an element contributes its {NV,DZ,OF,UF,NX} to the macro's pending flags if and only if it is active (vstart <= i < vl and its mask bit set) and the operation raises flags; contributions fold in ascending element order and are published on a per-element trace; the pending flags become architectural only at retire, a flush before that discards them, and a squashed macro contributes nothing. An inactive element performs no source access and no FPU operation at all, which the case checks by requiring the FPU issue count to equal the active-element count. THE DETERMINISM TABLE is the package's most reusable product and it is implemented as a table rather than a tolerance: results are compared with == (never an epsilon) for the element-wise arithmetic, min/max, sign injection, all comparisons, all element-wise conversions, the min/max reductions and the ORDERED reductions; and only the unordered reductions are compared by membership in an enumerated permitted set that covers every binary-tree shape over the active elements at both permitted internal precisions plus the specification's signed-zero allowance. The ordered case is caught by construction: the chosen operands (1.0, 2^24, 1.0, -2^24) make the left fold 0 and a reassociated fold 1, and the case asserts that the two differ AND that the DUT is not the reassociated value -- so a machine that reassociates an ordered reduction fails rather than passing within an epsilon. Four mutants each exit 1 with a name: INACTIVE_FLAG (a masked-off sNaN polluting NV), EARLY_COMMIT (flags architectural at completion instead of retire), REDUCE_REASSOC and RM_IGNORE (rounding mode ignored). ACT4 stays 127/127 and all eight sibling cases pass. NOT covered, stated by the lane: the vector FP unit is not wired into the core (the driver stands in for retire); no phase drives a non-zero vstart into this unit, whose only use of it is the active-range gate (restart is I-057's); the descriptor is not driven by this unit; vfredusum is implemented as the ordered serial fold, which the specification permits and the permitted-set comparator accepts; and throughput and the lane quota are I-058/I-059.

I-058.notes: Vector chaining with execution decoupled from commit. Case PASS from a clean build: 184 checks, three producer completion orders (ascending, descending and interleaved), and a MEASURED benefit in the RESULT line: 10 cycles with chaining against 18 without, 8 forwarded elements against 0, 1 stall against 9, with the architectural state identical on and off (verified here). THE SCOREBOARD IS PARALLEL, NOT AN EXTENSION OF THE DESCRIPTOR BITMAP, and the reason is the sharpest design distinction in the vector work so far: the descriptor's bitmap is ARCHITECTURAL progress bound to the I-057 restart point and must never record a speculative or wrong-path packet, while chaining readiness is a MICROARCHITECTURAL forwarding fact that has to carry element data and the producing generation and advances on an element write rather than on commit. The two cannot disagree because when the binding input is set, the descriptor's element-done pulse IS the network's accepted-packet pulse -- so only a correct-generation, in-vl, non-faulted packet advances either. BOTH NAMED HAZARDS ARE CONTROLLED: MACRO_READY (a macro-level ready bit letting a consumer read an element its producer has not written -- the card's first fail mode) and STALE_PACKET (a cancelled instruction's packet accepted by a new descriptor, which is the identity discipline the store queue, the TLB and the MSHR each needed), plus WAR_RELEASE (a source released while a younger macro still reads it) and REORDER (elements reordered within one macro). ACT4 was re-run at 127/127 from the committed driver. NOT covered, stated by the lane: the vector unit is still not wired into the core (mosaic_core.sv and mosaic_dispatch.sv contain zero references to any mosaic_vec module -- stated explicitly rather than implied); the lane-quota broker and the 2/4/8-lane switch are I-059's and the LLB is I-060's; sustained throughput is not claimed (one element per cycle, no parallel lanes); the generation identity is supplied by the driver rather than read from the macro's ROB generation output; the WAR arbiter port carries no generation; there are only two consumer slots and one group per consumer; interrupts and non-zero-vstart chaining are not exercised; and there is no formal equivalence proof. TWO PROCESS INCIDENTS from this window are recorded rather than dropped: the lane proved that a red `core.act_dut` was NOT its change by rebuilding the same case from `git show HEAD:` (a model of how to exonerate a suspect), and a peer's pathless `git stash` swept its tracked edits into a stash, which were restored hash-verified. The pathless-stash hazard is now a rule: a stash takes every modified tracked file in the repository, so it must always carry an explicit pathspec.

I-060.notes: The strictly restricted clean-copy locality buffer, registered p1-only because p0's RAM is non-cacheable and only the bypass path would run there (verified here from a deleted build directory: hit=29 miss=14 bypass=3 fill=37 fill_refused=3 inv=23 race_refuse=8 over 104 cycles). THE ENUMERATION IS THE DELIVERABLE, because the plan's own argument is that this structure is legal only when its invalidation sources can be listed -- and eight are: this hart's store or AMO commit (matching the physical line), an L1 refill or replacement, an external writer's snoop, a broadcast shootdown, FENCE, FENCE.I, SFENCE.VMA (which removes exactly the named ASID and/or page and is never treated as a memory-data fence), and a context change such as a satp write or an ASID switch (a full flush, because ASID numbers may be reused for a different address space). KEYING: the lookup key is the physical line plus the permission context {asid, leaf permissions} with NO VIRTUAL ADDRESS IN IT -- the vpn is stored only so that a by-page SFENCE.VMA can match -- and data-line invalidations deliberately ignore the context so a store removes every context's copy of the same physical line, while context-line invalidations match ASID and/or page. THE IN-FLIGHT RULE IS STATED AND CHECKED: a cycle that invalidates an entry grants no hit on it, the refusal being combinational with priority over the tag match and the entry clearing on the same rising edge; the case drives all eight sources in the same cycle as a lookup on that line and requires hit=0 and the entry removed, and it also checks the refusal is SPECIFIC (a lookup on a different line still hits in the same cycle as a store elsewhere) -- so the mechanism is not a blanket stall. FIVE mutants each exit 1 with a recorded hash and a named first failure: STORE_NO_INVALIDATE (the card's central fail mode), MMIO_HIT (a device access served from the buffer), RACE_STALE_HIT (the refusal removed, returning the pre-store value after the store is visible), ASID_SWITCH_NO_INVALIDATE and VA_KEYED (the alias case, which is why the key must be physical). THE CASE ASSERTS THE BUFFER ACTUALLY HIT BEFORE EACH INVALIDATION IT TESTS, which is what stops it from passing by accident: an LLB that returns the right value because the consumer re-read memory is not doing its job. ACT4 was re-run from a fresh build and stays 127/127; gates green (make check, lint p0 and p1 at 59 files clean, slang, check_records, check_exclusions and its controls). NOT covered, stated by the lane: the module is not instantiated in the core, so there is no real fill/store/fence wiring and no load-queue-violation or replay rule; single hart, so the snoop and shootdown interfaces are exercised as interfaces a coherence protocol would drive rather than as a real shootdown, and DMA, device and debugger masters are absent; a refill is a pulse rather than the L1; the permission-context key is conservative (it over-misses rather than under-invalidating, which is the safe direction but costs hits); the ordering rule has directed checks and a control but no formal proof; and the generation-validate-to-retire alternative design is not implemented. One housekeeping note: the lane removed a stale unregistered build directory that was shadowing the current core testbench header -- regenerable, not source. SECOND CASE, SAME TASK, and the one that supplies the LOCOMOTION half of the plan's measured-on-equal-resources requirement. The LLB and the prefetcher are in the core's data path (behind a default-off switch), with all EIGHT invalidation sources driven from the core itself -- store/AMO commit at the endpoint, L1 refill/replacement from the cache's own line traffic, an external snoop, a shootdown, FENCE, FENCE.I, SFENCE.VMA by ASID and/or page from the system unit's writeback pulse, and a satp/context change -- and the prefetcher observing demand at the cache's line request (PC from a functional ROB read port, address and context latched with the access) and egressing through the SAME bridge the cache uses with cache priority, so it is not a fourth arbiter master. THE STEP TABLE IS THE DELIVERABLE, one variable at a time on equal resources and verified here: baseline 3016 cycles / 394 dmem / 97 line-memory / 0 LLB hits / 0 prefetches; LLB only 2236 / 126 / 30 / 67 hits; prefetch only 3159 / 446 / 97 / 0 hits / 13 issued and ZERO useful; both 2223 / 126 / 17 / 80 hits / 13 issued and THIRTEEN USEFUL. Architecture identical in all four (the retirement stream through the park loop and all four signature words, checked against the program's own arithmetic). TWO FINDINGS IN THAT TABLE ARE WORTH MORE THAN THE FASTEST NUMBER: the prefetcher ALONE is SLOWER than the baseline (3159 against 3016) with zero useful prefetches -- the honest negative I-063 had already reported on p0, now reproduced in the machine -- while the prefetcher WITH the LLB is useful for every one of its 13 issues, because the LLB is where a prefetch's value is realised. Neither structure alone tells the truth about the pair, which is exactly why the plan insists on changing one variable at a time. THE SCHEDULER (I-062) IS DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED, with a precise reason rather than a shrug: the QoS module is a self-contained service model with its own three-class queues, arrival timestamps and windowed eligibility, while the core's data-memory arbiter is a hand-written single-outstanding ownership mux that both grants and routes; composing them would replace the ownership model with the QoS window model and re-derive response routing and PTW priority -- a second service model, which the card forbids. That is the same decision the fabric integration made about its arbiter, and it is recorded the same way. Four controls each exit 1 with a recorded hash: PERM_BYPASS (the store's read-for-ownership consulting the buffer where it must not), STORE_NO_INVALIDATE (the load after an AMO reading 0x64 where memory holds 0x69), the prefetcher's own PERM_BYPASS (a prefetch presented one line past the top of RAM) and ARCH_DATA (the retirement stream differing when the structures are on). ACT4 stays 127/127 (verified here) and lint is 63 sources clean. NOT covered, stated by the lane: this is the locality half of I-084 and NOT I-084 itself -- with the structures in the path the full comparison can now change one variable at a time across steering, locality and fusion on equal resources, and that is the plan's actual success criterion; the numbers are a measurement of this program and this geometry; and the scheduler remains unwired for the reason above.

I-059a.notes: THE VECTOR UNIT IS WIRED INTO THE CORE, and a decoded vector instruction now executes on the integrated machine. Case PASS from a clean build (verified here): 49 checks, four phases, 5 vector macros issued, 203 vector cycles against 103 scalar -- the vector path is SLOWER on this program, reported as a finding rather than hidden, and expected because the vector register file is not renamed and vector macros are serialised by an allocation barrier. WHAT WAS WIRED, one step at a time with ACT4 held at 127/127 between steps: OP-V structural decode (vsetvli/vsetivli/vsetvl, unit-stride vector loads and stores, vadd/vsub/vand/vor/vxor in vv/vx/vi) with ONE MACRO PER INSTRUCTION -- the rule the whole vector design rests on; dispatch routing through the system insert port with an allocation barrier; the vector CSRs (vl, vtype, vlenb, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr) on the core's CSR path with mstatus.VS dirtying recorded per ROB slot and applied at retirement; vector macros resolving at the ROB head like system macros and completing once on writeback port 3; precise faults with vstart written through the configuration unit and a restart keeping the committed prefix; the descriptor bound to the ROB identity; the chain as the element-packet validator; and the whole engine (cfg, descriptor, VRF, ALU, LSU, restart, chain) instantiated in the core with the packetizer's memory port as a FOURTH OWNER on the single data arbiter. FIVE CONTROLS each exit 1 with a recorded hash and a named first failure: VEC_RETIRE_INCOMPLETE (retiring with element progress unfinished), VEC_STALE_PACKET (a packet from a cancelled macro accepted by its successor), VEC_IGNORE_VS_OFF (executing while mstatus.VS forbids it), the whole-macro-trap mutant carried from I-057, and a structural companion on the chaining case. A REAL ISA DEFECT WAS FOUND AND FIXED BY THIS PACKAGE, and the story of how it was nearly missed is worth more than the fix: the first attempt reported that the handler's first 'csrr mtval' returned 0 while a later read returned the right value, and hypothesised a trap-entry staging latency (a defect any handler would hit). The retry proved that hypothesis false with evidence -- the CSR write path is one write in one cycle, the core's own o_trap_tval and o_csr_mtval agreed, and the handler's FIRST read returned the right value -- and found instead that the check's own failure MESSAGE printed run.Slot(16) (an untouched word, always 0) while the condition tested run.Slot(2). The testbench was lying about which word it had examined. Behind that artifact was the genuine defect: mosaic_core.sv computed the vector fault's mtval as base + (vstart << eew_sew) where eew_sew is log2(EEW in BITS) while the packetizer addresses in BYTES, so the byte offset is vstart << (eew_sew - 3). For the case (e32, vstart=2) the machine named base+64 where the faulting element sits at base+8 -- wrong by exactly the factor of eight that shifting bits instead of bytes produces, and any handler computing from mtval for a vector memory fault would have been handed an address eight elements further on. One term, fixed, and the handler now reads the faulting element's own address. The tb's misleading messages were fixed with it, which is the real lesson: a diagnostic that names a plausible defect (a staging latency) and prints a value that supports it sent the first attempt's analysis in the wrong direction for its whole duration. ACT4 stays 127/127 (verified here) and FORTY-ONE cases were re-run green, including both profiles of the privilege, translation, boot, trap and memory cases and all eight sibling vector cases. NOT covered, stated by the lane: only the decoded subset reaches the engine (other vector families are refused at decode); mosaic_vec_fp is not instantiated; width suffixes that disagree with vtype.SEW are refused; vector memory has no Sv39 translation or L1 path; VECTOR REGISTERS ARE NOT RENAMED, so vector macros are serialised by the barrier and a cross-macro chaining hazard is structurally unreachable; and the lane broker and quotas are untouched (I-059's own card territory, which is why this integration is recorded as its own entry).

I-059.notes: Runtime lane-quota reallocation -- the plan's dynamic-aggregation story, and the card whose ID was deliberately kept open while the engine integration was recorded as I-059a. Case PASS from a clean build (verified here): 111 checks over seven phases, 32 elements attributed at quota 8 and 32 at quota 4 with none left over (lane4_high_elems=0), two resizes each with its own acknowledgement, lint 60 sources clean. THE RULE IS THE ONE THE CARD DEMANDS: the quota changes HOW MANY LANES WORK ON THE ELEMENTS, NEVER WHICH ELEMENTS EXIST. A request is latched and committed only through the ownership FSM's sequence -- stop admitting new macros, drain the staged macro, the launched macro's element work and any uncollected completion to zero, then the engine's own acknowledgement (idle AND no valid AND no pending writeback), then publish with a generation increment -- and the element-to-lane plan is a LAUNCH-TIME SNAPSHOT so a lane that goes away cannot change the running macro's elements. vl and vlenb never move: the broker has no path to the configuration unit at all, which is a structural way of meeting the card's second fail mode rather than a check that could be forgotten. WHAT WAS REUSED RATHER THAN REINVENTED is worth recording: mosaic_owner_fsm (I-031) is instantiated, not copied; the runtime lane count of the VRF and the descriptor come from I-053; per-lane attribution reads the chain's accepted element packets (I-058); and I-031's own NO_ACK mutant is reused as the no-acknowledgement control. Four mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure: DISCARD_REST (a resize discarding the in-flight macro's remaining elements -- the card's first fail mode), VLEN_LEAK (a resize changing the visible vector length -- the second), MID_MACRO (a resize applied mid-macro instead of at the boundary) and the reused NO_ACK. ACT4 stays 127/127. THE HONEST LIMIT, stated by the lane and more important than the pass: the core has one VRF read slot and one ALU lane, so '8 lanes' is an element-to-lane ATTRIBUTION plus the lane-count input rather than eight parallel datapaths -- the case proves the PROTOCOL and the INVARIANCE, not a throughput gain, and a throughput or area comparison needs real parallel lanes. 'Two workloads' is one hart with two register regions and two descriptor chains interleaved by the program, not two harts; a multi-hart version needs a cohort-owned lane pool with cross-hart drain arbitration and a per-hart or replicated register file. In-flight packet migration is explicitly unsupported (the plan names it a separate experiment). And I-084's comparison CAN now include a lane-quota dimension -- this case supplies its identical-architecture precondition -- but only as throughput and area once parallel lanes exist, which is exactly the distinction the plan's 'measured, not inherited' rule is about. Registry note: the lane added the two new modules to the build list of the 30 cases that instantiate the core -- a build-manifest necessity, with no status or ownership change and the pending marker left for the lead.

I-061.notes: Same-hart line coalescing for the vector memory path. Case PASS from a clean build (verified here): 675 checks over 44 cells, 12 merged groups, and a measured request reduction from 94 to 28 -- a factor of 3.4, and the number that rules out the silent failure of a coalescer that never merges. THE MERGEABILITY RULE IS A CONJUNCTION, each term of which is checked: coalescing enabled, the macro is not an atomic class, the macro is not an ordered form, the item is unit-stride or constant-stride, EVERY byte it enables is normal memory as the GENERATED platform map defines it (mosaic_pa_normal = idempotent and not device, emitted by gen_manifest from each region's own fields -- never a hand-written list, which is the rule the cache and LLB packages each had to learn), and for a store its bytes are disjoint from the group's. A group is one 8-byte beat carrying the union of its members' byte masks -- the memory port's transaction, not a cache line, and the report says so rather than implying a line merge. THE FAULT RULE IS THE SHARPEST REQUIREMENT AND IS MET BY CONSTRUCTION: a fault on a coalesced group DE-COALESCES the group -- it is replayed element by element in element order -- so vstart still names the faulting element and only the elements before it take effect, which is exactly the element granularity I-056 established and the card insists must survive merging. THE STORE-ORDERING RULE COMES FROM THE INSTRUCTION TYPE, as the card demands: element order, required by the ISA for the ordered forms and chosen for the unordered forms because it is the only order under which the coalesced and uncoalesced results are identical -- and the coalescer never has to pick a winner at all, because overlapping-byte stores are never merged into one request, while a disjoint pair inside one beat does merge. Four mutants each exit 1 with a recorded hash and a named first failure: COALESCE_MASK_LOSS (a group losing a member's byte mask), COALESCE_GROUP_FAULT (a group fault reported for the whole group instead of the element), COALESCE_DEVICE (a device access merged) and COALESCE_STORE_ORDER (a same-address pair applied out of the declared order). I-056's four mutants are still caught, so the packetizer's own rules survived the change. ACT4 stays 127/127 WITH THE COALESCER ENABLED IN THE CORE, and all twelve p0 vector cases plus vec.integrated pass. A PRE-EXISTING DEFECT WAS FOUND AND RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED, which is the right call for a package that was not asked to touch it: a probe during the coalescing work found that an uncoalesced load still in flight when a stop is taken is DISCARDED rather than written back, because the writeback push is gated by the abort signal -- a stop-path behaviour belonging to I-057's territory, now on the record with the mechanism named so its owner can judge whether it matters. NOT covered, stated by the lane: the indexed, segmented, whole-register and mask modes are deliberately not coalesced (unit-stride and constant-stride are, in both directions); the merge is per 8-byte beat, so a cache-line merge is neither implemented nor claimed; no same-beat mixed normal/device case is constructible from the shipped maps because every region boundary is 8-byte aligned; no interaction with the LLB (it exists as a module but is not in the core path); single hart; no performance claim beyond the request count; and no masked coalesced run in the case's matrix.

I-062.notes: Criticality-aware memory arbitration. Case PASS from a clean build under p0 and p1 (verified here: 112152 per-cycle checks over 6819 cycles). THREE CLASSES, derived from the request's own identity rather than a side channel: SCALAR (a latency-critical dependent load, with a reservation floor of 4 grants in a window of 8), PREFETCH (a placeholder until I-063 exists, bounded to 2) and BULK (vector streaming, ceiling 2 so it cannot monopolise). THE THREE MECHANISMS THE CARD NAMES ARE ALL PRESENT AND SEPARATELY CONTROLLED: a windowed scalar reservation whose exactness is argued in the module header and whose measured share equals the quota in every phase; a bulk ceiling that normal grants never exceed, so an over-quota grant must be a REPORTED age escape; and age-based escape as the only over-quota path (17 grants in the directed age phase after a 32-cycle wait, 48 in the stress mix). THE SERVICE ASSUMPTION IS THE STANDARD I-030 SET, met in full: written into the module header ('while work is pending the memory port is not ready for more than 4 consecutive cycles'), exposed as an observation with a sticky violation flag, checked every cycle in every phase, and asserted in BOTH directions by a directed phase that holds the port not-ready for 7 cycles and requires the flag -- and a declared waiting bound of 212 cycles is computed from the geometry and checked against every measured wait. THE MEASUREMENTS ARE p50/p99, as the card asks: in the chain phase a scalar dependent chain against 100% bulk gives SCALAR 2/6 and BULK 27/27; under the saturation mix SCALAR 11/32 and BULK 23/33; every maximum is below the bound. THE STIMULUS PROVABLY REACHES THE CARD'S FAIL MODE, which is what makes the pass mean something: with the policy off the scalar dependent chain advances ZERO links over 800 cycles while bulk is served 400 times, and an independent naive model replaying the same offer stream leaves SCALAR and PREFETCH stuck at 0 of 4 while BULK takes 1200. PRIORITY DOES NOT CHANGE A RESULT: a fixed 200-request mixed stream replayed policy-off and policy-on delivers all 200 payloads identical with the SERVICE ORDER differing -- the order changes, the data does not. Four mutants each exit 1 with a recorded hash and a named first failure: SCALAR_STARVE, BULK_MONOPOLY, NO_AGE_ESCAPE (caught BY THE BOUND and not by a timeout, which is the card's own prohibition) and DATA (a corrupted payload). AN HONEST SCOPE NOTE RATHER THAN A DECORATIVE REUSE: mosaic_arbiter.sv (I-030) is in the compiled source list but is NOT instantiated, because its completion-path geometry and its immediate quota-exhaustion escape make the very starvation this card asks to demonstrate impossible -- the lane reused I-030's bounded-service MODEL (the windowed quota, the exactness argument, the per-class FIFO with backpressure, the checked assumption and the bound shape) and said so, rather than instantiating a second service model for appearance. NOT covered, stated by the lane: the scheduler is module-level and not wired into the core's memory path (integration is separate work); the PREFETCH class is a placeholder until I-063; the numbers are a measurement of this geometry and this traffic mix, not of a general memory system; and no area or timing claim is made.

I-063.notes: The reuse predictor and switchable prefetch, closing the memory-path block. Case PASS from a clean build (verified here: 13 prefetches -- 5 useful, 2 useless, 1 late, 1 cancelled -- against 56 demand reads over 94 cycles; lint 62 sources clean). THE CARD'S SEQUENCING REQUIREMENT IS MET LITERALLY: the workload's characteristics were recorded with prediction DISABLED and before it was enabled at all, from the DUT's own observation counters -- 18 accesses, 3 new PCs, 15 repeats, 8 stride matches, 4 mismatches, 3 zero strides, 6 reuse hits, 0 issued -- so the predictor's expected benefit is a measurement rather than a guess with a state machine attached. THE USEFULNESS HISTOGRAM CONSERVES, which is what makes it a report rather than a decoration: on p1 the 13 issued prefetches are exactly 5 useful + 2 useless + 1 late + 1 cancelled + 4 in-flight, and on p0 (whose RAM is non-cacheable, so nothing can be prefetched usefully) 22 issued are 0 useful + 20 useless + 1 late + 1 cancelled -- AN HONEST NEGATIVE REPORTED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: on that profile the predictor is pure overhead, twenty wasted reads and zero benefit, and the record says so. THE HARM BOUND HAS BOTH HALVES THE CARD DEMANDS, each with its own control: a wrong prediction adds latency or traffic but can never introduce an architectural fault or an irreversible device read (the prefetch goes through the SAME permission, alias and cacheability checks as any demand access, and the DEVICE_READ and PERM_BYPASS mutants are caught), and prediction can never become the only source of correctness (the on/off architectural identity is checked, and the ARCH_DATA mutant that changes a result is caught, as is CANCEL_LANDS -- a cancelled prefetch whose data arrives anyway, which would violate the same rule the LLB proves for cancelled accesses). Four mutants each exit 1 with a named first failure; ACT4 stays 127/127. NOT covered, stated by the lane: the prefetcher and the LLB are both module-level and NOT in the core path -- 'prefetch into the LLB' is an interaction the driver wires, and no real load flows through either -- so this is a harm-bound proof, not a performance result; NO ENERGY CLAIM IS MADE, because the card explicitly forbids inferring one from a hit rate, and only the traffic delta is measured; predictor accuracy is measured on directed stride streams only, and the p0 run shows the failure mode the card warns about (pure pollution); single hart; and the LLB's eight invalidation sources and in-flight ordering rule remain I-060's own evidence rather than being re-proven here.

I-084.verdict: PASS -- and this is the package that satisfies the plan's measured-on-equal-resources criterion
I-084.notes: THE EQUAL-RESOURCE COMPARISON, and the plan's actual success criterion for this project's differentiated half: not a feature list but a measurement, one variable at a time, with the fixed and dynamic configurations measured rather than assumed. Case PASS from a clean build (verified here, p1): three workloads across seven configurations -- baseline, +steering, +locality, +prefetch, +both, +coalescing, +lane quota -- with exactly one variable changed per configuration and the cache path held high in all of them. RESOURCES ARE ASSERTED EQUAL PER CELL AND ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL ACROSS ALL 21 CELLS, read from the core's OWN evidence ports rather than restated: 64 ROB entries, 8 issue-queue entries, 96 PRF entries in 4 banks, 2 clusters, a 32-byte 8-set 1-way L1, 8 lanes, an 8-entry reset window and vlenb 16 -- which is the card's fail mode ('a comparison that secretly changes the resource count to make the dynamic configuration look better') made detectable, and shown falsifiable by a mutant that drifts a resource. ARCHITECTURAL IDENTITY holds in all seven configurations -- the retire stream field by field through the park loop, all four signature words and the memory result -- and is shown falsifiable by a mutant that drifts the architecture. ENGAGEMENT IS CHECKED PER CONFIGURATION with the NO_DELTA idea: each configuration's own counter must be non-zero on its primary workload and the baseline's must be inert, so a table that reports a difference where none exists is caught. THE NEGATIVES ARE IN THE TABLE RATHER THAN AVERAGED AWAY, which is the point: on the streaming workload +prefetch ALONE is 143 cycles SLOWER than the baseline with zero of thirteen prefetches useful, while +both is 793 cycles FASTER with thirteen of thirteen useful; +coalescing costs five cycles on the vector workload even though the data-memory count falls from 40 to 22 (six elements merged); +steering is exactly neutral on the short ALU chain (396 grants, 0 cycles) while the fabric measurement had it balancing the clusters at neutral cost there too; and +lane-quota is zero cycles with the element-to-lane attribution moving to a different set of lanes (share changes WHICH lanes work, not how much work exists -- the property the lane broker's own package established). A table averaged over configurations would have hidden the prefetcher-alone pessimisation entirely, which is why the card says one variable at a time. 132 checks; ACT4 stays 127/127 (verified here). I-031's dynamic-ownership FSM is compiled but deliberately NOT instantiated, so RESOURCE RECONFIGURATION AND OWNERSHIP CHANGE ARE NOT PART OF THIS COMPARISON -- stated in the report, because a reader could otherwise conclude that reconfiguration was demonstrated. NOT covered, also stated: no area, Fmax, network-bytes, tail-latency or power claim; one seed and one profile (p1, because p0's RAM is non-cacheable and the locality configurations are inert there, which is why this case is registered p1-only); +steering is a single toggle gating three structures, with per-structure isolation living in I-090's step table; and the coalescing negative rests on one short workload.

I-064.notes: TWO ARCHITECTURAL DOMAINS ON ONE PHYSICAL MACHINE -- the plan's premise made real, and the first time anything in this project has tested that two domains can coexist without corrupting each other. Case PASS under profile p3 (the two-hart profile) from a clean build, verified here by the integration lead: RESULT PASS multihart.isolation. THE CONSTRUCTION: independent PC, rename tables, ROB, CSRs, load/store queues and interrupt state per hart, with the memory and cache service shared, statically partitioned as the card requires for a first cut, and EVERY PACKET CARRYING ITS HART OWNERSHIP so a response is matched to the identity that asked rather than to arrival order -- the same identity discipline the store queue, the TLB, the MSHR and the chaining network each needed. THE ISOLATION PROPERTIES THE CARD NAMES are the acceptance criteria and each has its control: a fault or a flush in one hart does not lose the other hart's in-flight requests or state; NO GLOBAL REDIRECT clears the other hart (the card's first fail mode); and hart-identity reuse cannot confuse a response (the second). The case runs DIFFERENT programs with different ASIDs on the two harts -- deliberately different, because two identical programs on two harts would pass with the domains cross-wired -- and compares each hart's retirement stream and signature against its own reference, while a shared-structure counter shows both harts actually used the same memory service. The single-hart machine is unchanged: lint is 64 sources clean and core.mem_program still passes with the two-hart module present. THE RECORD KEEPS TWO NOTES IT SHOULD NOT HIDE: (1) this is STATIC partitioning -- the plan's dynamic sharing, migration and reconfiguration are later work, and I-031's ownership FSM remains compiled but not instantiated, so nothing here claims dynamic resource movement; (2) the lane's edits were swept into the integration lead's commit by a `git add -A` while the lane was still running, which is a process slip this ledger has recorded once before -- the state happened to be green when swept and the lead re-verified it (lint 64/64, core.mem_program PASS, this case PASS) before recording, but the rule stands: commit only what has been verified, and never with `-A` while another lane is mid-edit.

V-061.notes: Delivered as a second campaign in sim/unit/tb_llb.cpp (main branches on --case), reusing the I-060 Harness/host-memory oracle. Lead re-ran the case: RESULT PASS llb.freshness_and_ownership llb-fresh: hit=31 miss=17 bypass=6 fill=31 fill_refused=12 inv=14 race_refuse=1 checks=0 cycles=107. NOTE ON THAT LINE: checks=0 is a reporting defect in this harness, not a coverage statement -- rep_->checks() is not the counter the harness's Require wrapper increments (the pre-existing llb.stale_copy_invalidation case prints checks=0 for the same reason), so the ledger does NOT quote a check count from it. What proves the stimulus arrived is the case's own coverage requirements, which PASS: hits, misses, bypasses, fills, refused fills and invalidations each moved a counter, and every hit is compared word-for-word against an independent memory oracle with every resident entry checked at rest. Five controls, each rebuilt from a deleted build directory with its -D on the Verilator command line and in -CFLAGS, all exit 1 with a named first failure and a binary hash distinct from the shipping fb6b1dd90314ddab: STORE_NO_INVALIDATE 1bbb8fa57ee907f0 (local-writer-freshness), MMIO_HIT 14cb02cd088b60ba (hit-miss-bypass), RACE_STALE_HIT 7b55ede690dd7ec4 (misprediction-race/hit-store), ASID_SWITCH_NO_INVALIDATE babc65022ef8d729 (ownership-context-change), VA_KEYED 8eec1f8401f87e90 (same-address-aliasing). GAPS NAMED RATHER THAN CHECKED: lane reassignment / owner-domain transfer is NOT TESTED because mosaic_llb.sv has no owner, lane or domain field or port (its key is {physical line, ASID, leaf permissions}), the lane broker does not connect to it, and the LLB is not instantiated in mosaic_core.sv -- there is no mechanism to drive or observe a leaked owner's data, so no check was invented; version/generation checking is untestable because no version field exists (the design takes the conservative flush-and-refuse path); there is no invalidation-acknowledgement port, so same-cycle removal is checked as the closest observable; cross-hart shootdown, DMA/device-master topologies, the prefetcher and o_evict_valid_o are not driven in a single-hart harness (snoop ports stand in); a non-idempotent-but-cacheable region would not be excluded (the LLB gates on mosaic_pa_cacheable, and the map agreement that makes that sufficient IS checked). No RTL changed by this package.

V-062.notes: Lead re-ran the case: RESULT PASS cache.coalescer_boundaries coalescer: miss=18 coalesce=9 refill=8 fault=1 wb=1 reads=9 writes=1 cycles=108 | cancel-keeps-others (85 checks, p1; p1 because p0's RAM is non-cacheable, which would make the MMIO/AMO bypass clause vacuous). The card's enumeration is covered where the port can express it: same line different bytes -> merged with each waiter answered its own word; duplicate bytes -> merged and answered once; cross line sharing set+offset (low 8 bits equal) -> NOT merged, two entries and two reads; cross page -> NOT merged; MMIO and AMO -> NOT merged, both bypass the cache and memory sees the exact transaction (a cacheable non-atomic control shows the bypass clause is non-vacuous); a coalesced fault -> per-consumer fault answers with no install and a successful retry; cancelling one of two coalesced consumers leaves the survivor answered once with its own word. Four controls, each from a deleted build directory, each exit 1 with a named first failure and a binary hash distinct from the shipping 9623e30f8a072eb1: COALESCE_LOW_BITS 7afbe386c2be7d03 ('cross-line-same-set: two different lines are two entries'), STORE_MASK_DROP eca1f9a654f77c26 ('store-byte-merge: only the selected byte lanes changed'), WRONG_WAITER e8904a65b26e6c77 ('same-line-different-bytes: word 1 returned to its own request'), FAULT_VALID ed1986620a1e5057 ('coalesced-fault-per-request: every consumer is faulted, not just the first'). NOT COVERED, with the reason rather than a check that passes: differing permissions (no permission or PMT field on the cache's request port -- permission is raised upstream in the LSU/PMP), same-VA/different-PA and same-PA/different-VA (the coalescer key is a physical line with no VA field; covered at the LLB by V-061's same-address-aliasing campaign), ordering incompatibility beyond the AMO class (no ordering tag on the port; aq/rl tied off), same-byte write-write ordering and store merge across eviction, cross-hart coalescing (V-070) and formal proof. The lead also re-ran the two cases this lane could not build while another lane held mosaic_core.sv: amo.linearization PASS and cache.integrated_path PASS. NOTE: the shared cache testbench now elaborates an inert access-path instance, so the binary hashes cited in the I-042/I-043 reports are historical; their checks and traces are unchanged.

V-064.notes: Lead re-ran the case: RESULT PASS multihart.context_isolation h0=157 h1=12100 retires, fcsr=0x0000000000000010/0x0000000000000028 vl=1/3 seed=1 (41 checks, p3, seven Pass clauses covered). A REAL DEFECT WAS FOUND AND FIXED, not worked around: mosaic_csr read mhartid from the single generated constant MOSAIC_CSR_RESET_MHARTID and mosaic_core never wired HART_ID into it, so BOTH harts read 0 -- architecturally wrong for any multi-hart machine, since mhartid is a hart's own identifier. Fix: mosaic_csr gains a MHARTID_VALUE parameter whose default is the generated constant (single-hart builds stay bit-identical) and mosaic_core passes CORE_XLEN'(HART_ID); the shared-id behaviour survives only inside the MOSAIC_MUTANT_MHARTID_SHARED control branch. Three controls, each from a deleted build directory with a hash distinct from the shipping 26486c13bea91c5921c886b97239f97418076fbc4473ee52a582f9b08eb61015 and exit 1 with a named first failure: MOSAIC_MUTANT_MHARTID_SHARED 520c54d2cd4a9b27... ('hart 0 reads mhartid 0 and hart 1 reads mhartid 1'), MOSAIC_MH_CTX_MUTANT_HALT_ALL 487e9b16a4efedcc... ('hart 1 retired its program and parked'), and a driver-level --control-share-ref which compares hart 1 against hart 0's reference -- the card's own named failure mode, one shared reference state -- exit 1 with 'MISMATCH stream/h1'. The change was re-verified against every case it can move, each from a deleted build directory: core.act_dut (p1) PASS, core.corpus_sweep (p1) PASS, csr.precise_trap_mret (p0) PASS, core.trap_csr_program (p0) PASS, multihart.isolation (p3) PASS, lint_rtl 65/65 on both profiles. No ACT4 or corpus program reads mhartid, so no golden moved. NOT COVERED, with reasons: no 4-hart configuration (the wrapper hardcodes two harts and p3 declares two), no interrupt-controller topology (the IRQ is a self-raised mip/mie software interrupt, not CLINT/PLIC routing), instruction fetch is not translated in this core so 'the same PC' is a physical PC, no cross-hart memory ordering or coherence (disjoint pages; V-065..V-067 own it), vector register state is observed only through a vector store (vmv.x.s is not wired), and halt causes other than WFI plus park.

I-044.blocking_defect: D5: a store refused by PMP raises NO store access fault. A store is authorised and retired before it is presented to the memory endpoint, so the endpoint's refusal is counted by the store queue and never reaches the ROB; s-store-deny-w and u-store-deny-w retire the program's ecall with cause 9/8 where the ISA requires 7, and lock-deny-m-store and mprv-store-uses-mpp produce no trap at all. Nothing is written in any of the four -- the card's 'no side effect on a fault' half holds; the missing half is the fault itself. The correct fix is non-speculative and changes the store queue's authorisation contract, which is why the lane left it to its owners rather than patching the memory path under four delivered cases.
I-044.defects_fixed_in_these_attempts: Four, each with its reproduction: (D1) the NAPOT match compared the free address bits instead of the fixed ones, so a NAPOT entry matched about one word of its region -- found because a verifiably installed code-region entry was followed by an S-mode fetch inside it trapping with cause 1 and a zero deny counter; (D2) the supervisor-CSR decode arm never raised addr_impl, so every S-mode CSR read as unimplemented -- found as csrw scounteren from M trapping with cause 2 in the bootstrap; (D3) the read-only CSR encoding was applied to reads, refusing a U-mode cycle read that mcounteren+scounteren permit; (D4) an illegal MRET/SRET executed before its exception was taken, so mret in S-mode changed the privilege and redirected before trapping.
